#2212. Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

Thomas Tuchel says Cole Palmer is paying the price for his controversial withdrawal from England’s last camp.

The Chelsea forward was a notable omission from Tuchel’s squad for next week’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

He was originally named in Tuchel’s group for September and October’s matches but withdrew due to a minor injury, despite playing 90 minutes in Chelsea’s final match, much to the annoyance of the German, who said he “misses too many opportunities to impress”.

The 24-year-old then featured in all four of his club’s Premier League matches ahead of this camp, but was overlooked by Tuchel, who handed maiden call-ups to Jobe Bellingham and Josh King.

“I guess everyone is desperate to play for England, and Cole is no exception,” Tuchel said.

“We’re speaking now about the player who is not in camp, and it counts when you are in camp.

“And I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp. It was two and a half weeks, and the players and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary and that’s why the credit goes to them.

“The trust is for them. If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.

“So it’s not personal, and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country. But the competition is on, and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.

“The door is always open, but nothing has changed, and we decided to do this camp without him.”

Spain told to walk away from 2030 World Cup if Morocco gets final

Returning star makes 'up my game' admission amid striker battle

Aberdeen suffer major double blow as Stephen Robinson confirms injury lay-offs

Palmer was one of five withdrawals ahead of the last camp, with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Tino Livramento and Marcus Rashford also pulling out.

Rice is the only one of that quintet recalled as Tuchel reiterated that he will always give preference to those who “walk the talk”.

“The best reactions to the withdrawals in the last camp from the players who were in camp was just to put the quality in and make it a successful camp,” Tuchel said.

“That’s the best foundation for the next camp, to have less withdrawals, which is actually happening now.

“So it’s always about the ones who are in camp.

“It’s always the ones who don’t withdraw and who walk the talk and come to camp and show that it matters and put the quality in. And this is always what we will reward.

“That was always the message, very, very early, since we took charge, that it matters if you are in camp and it matters what you do in camp and the last camp was an excellent one, so the trust and the belief is in the players that were there.”

Mainoo was also overlooked, despite returning to Manchester United’s side.

“I think Kobbie had a difficult spell now with his team and his club, and missed a lot, a lot of matches,” Tuchel said.

“And in the meantime, it was Jobe who impressed in the same level of time, and that’s exactly what we want.

“The door is always open for younger ones to overtake or to make their mark.”

#2211. FacileRent Molinari Napoli, presentata la stagione 2026/27: sport, territorio e nuove ambizioni

– Passione, ambizione e vicinanza al territorio. All’insegna di questi aspetti la Molinari Napoli ha presentato il nuovo anno sportivo ed in particolare la stagione della squadra che competerà in Serie B2 femminile. Un evento – quello tenutosi sabato 7 novembre al PalaVesuvio – che ha coinvolto società, istituzioni, partner, staff tecnico e atlete, per raccontare obiettivi, ambizioni e prospettive di un progetto che vuole continuare a investire nello sport e nel territorio.

«Lavoriamo sul territorio da anni, avvicinando i giovani di Ponticelli allo sport. Da cinque anni sentiamo la vicinanza dell’Amministrazione comunale che ci ha aiutato in qualsiasi circostanza», ha dichiarato il Presidente della Molinari Napoli, Gennaro Nappo. «Per la Serie B2 c’è tanta ambizione, voglia di crescere e di essere d’esempio per il settore giovanile. Abbiamo costruito una squadra competitiva e speriamo che il campo ce lo dimostri».

Presenti alla conferenza l’On. Borrelli e l’Ass. Ferrante

«Io non credo più all’idea del centro e delle periferie per come si sta evolvendo il sistema sociale del nostro territorio. Ogni luogo come questo (il PalaVesuvio di Via Argine n.d.r.) è oro colato da valorizzare», ha dichiarato l’Onorevole Francesco Emilio Borrelli, presente alla conferenza stampa. «Lo sport è qualcosa di straordinario non solo perché ci insegna la disciplina, il rispetto del prossimo e l’impegno, ma anche perché ci spinge a fare attività fisica. Noi siamo in questo momento la Regione più obesa d’Italia per quanto riguarda i bambini. Bambini che non fanno sport: è importante fargli fare un’attività pulita e sana». Borrelli ha concluso il suo intervento sottolineando la vicinanza alla squadra: «Verrò sicuramente a vedere una delle vostre partite: tiferò per voi».

«Lo sport è una leva fondamentale, anche se a volte viene considerato secondario, soprattutto per quanto riguarda i supporti economici», ha dichiarato l’Assessora allo Sport ed alle Pari Opportunità del Comune di Napoli, Emanuela Ferrante. «Cinque anni fa, con grande difficoltà, ho provato a recuperare delle somme per riqualificare gli impianti, senza i quali non si può andare da nessuna parte. A conclusione di questo anno, che ha visto Napoli essere Capitale Europea dello Sport, posso dire con fierezza e con grande gioia che abbiamo investito 35 milioni di euro su tanti gli impianti sportivi. Partendo dagli impianti riqualificati si può ambire a realizzare quello che penso sia il diritto di tutti i ragazzi: fare sport».

L’Assessora si è rivolta poi direttamente alla squadra. «Siete una testimonianza ed un esempio per tutte le ragazze ed i ragazzi di Ponticelli. Questa stagione sarà una straordinaria esperienza e cercheremo di far riempire la palestra ogni volta che giocherete in casa».

#2210. Plymouth Argyle must eye January transfer move for 10-goal EFL striker: Opinion

Plymouth Argyle will get the opportunity to freshen up their ranks this winter with some reinforcements. PAFC are sat in 5th place in the League One table after their first 14 fixtures as they eye promotion back to the Championship.

The Pilgrims should target a move for Walsall striker Aaron Pressley to add more competition and depth to their attacking department. At the age of 25, he has already picked up a decent amount of EFL experience and he has potential to grow and develop further down the line.

Pressley, who is an ex-Scotland youth international, is a key player for the Saddlers and has proved in League Two that he knows where the back of the net is. He has made 15 appearances in all competitions for Lee Grant‘s side in this campaign, 12 of which have come in the league, and he has scored 10 goals already.

Plymouth Argyle are in the play-offs along with Oxford United, Luton Town and Reading as they chase down Huddersfield Town and Stockport County. They take on non-league Alvechurch at home in the FA Cup this weekend.

Plymouth Argyle sold key attacker Lorent Tolaj to Bristol City in the summer. PAFC have since missed his presence and goal scoring touch.

Welshman Will Evans was brought in as his replacement from Mansfield Town. However, he has only scored three times and hasn’t been prolific in Devon.

The Pilgrims are the lowest scorers in the top six and need to be more ruthless in front of goal. Therefore, signing another forward in January has to be a priority.

Pressley fits the bill for Plymouth Argyle and will be full of confidence at the moment. He is under contract at Walsall until June 2028 meaning he still has just under two years left to run down.

Standing at 6ft 4inc, Pressley is solid in the air and would give Plymouth Argyle another dimension going forward. He would be useful for PAFC to throw on if they needed a goal.

The Edinburgh-born man moved down to England from Hearts as a youngster and had spells at Aston Villa and Brentford in the Premier League. He has since had stints at AFC Wimbledon, Accrington Stanley, Stevenage and Barrow.

His move to Walsall in 2025 has worked out well for all parties and he is one of their most prized assets. The Saddlers could lose him soon though and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see other teams sniffing around him.

#2209. Sandro Mazzola, il figlio di Valentino. Dal Grande Torino alla Grande Inter

“Sandro Mazzola ha reso onore a Milano e ne ha accresciuto il prestigio”. Le parole dell'omelia di Carlo Faccendini, abate della basilica di Sant’Ambrogio, durante il funerale di Sandro Mazzola ha racchiuso quello che pensava la città del figlio di Valentino, inarrivabile nella sua epicità, anche se le classifiche fra la Grande Inter e il Grande Torino non sono semplici da eseguire. Forse è un esercizio di stile totalmente inutile, ma è chiaro che c'è una linea di continuità che parte da Cassano D'Adda, dove è nato il padre, per arrivare a Milano.

"Noi oggi abbiamo il dovere di preservarne la memoria e i suoi contenuti, da trasmettere obbligatoriamente a tutti i giovani, non solo quelli del nostro settore giovanile. Gli insegnamenti che lui ha lasciato rappresentano una palestra di vita per il futuro. Una leggenda della nostra Inter che se ne va, uno che ha generato emozioni per chi è appassionato di sport. Abbiamo questo dovere di conservazione e trasmissioni, perché in Mazzola si possono trovare tanti elementi che possono caratterizzare gli uomini del domani: umiltà, cultura del lavoro, senso d'appartenenza… Un viatico importante per il mondo giovanile".

"Ciao Sandro, grazie per l'eredità che ci lasci per il ricordo del tuo stile, della determinazione e caparbietà. Grazie per i gol bellissimi che ci hanno fatto gioire. Raggiungi i campioni della Grande Inter del cui prestigio godiamo ancora adesso. Troverai la pace dopo una vita tanto intensa e noi non ti scorderemo mai. Un bacio Massimo Moratti". Oggi Sandro Mazzola compirebbe 84 anni.

#2208. Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team

Neil McCann will continue his drive to see Kilmarnock “flourish” in the face of growing fan scrutiny.

The Ayrshire club are one point ahead of William Hill Premiership bottom side Hibernian, with nine points from 36 and having conceded 28 goals from 12 games amid concern and disgruntlement among a section of the Killie support.

McCann is preparing his players to take on a Celtic team who are four points ahead of Rangers at the top of the table, having played a game more and on the back of a morale-boosting 3-2 Europa League win over Besiktas on Thursday night

However, the Kilmarnock boss remains positive, and said: “Supporters will always give their opinion when they come into the stadium and they’ll voice it. They’re entitled to voice their opinion.

“My pressure, to be honest with you, is preparing our players tactically, physically, mentally.

Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission Spain told to walk away from 2030 World Cup if Morocco gets final

“And then when they take the field, I give them full autonomy to go and carry out all of those instructions, but play with the freedom and bravery that got us out of trouble last year.

“Nothing’s changed in my build-up. Nothing’s changed in my drive. Nothing’s changed in my approach to getting Kilmarnock to be a team that wants to put on a product on the pitch.

“A lot’s been made of ‘you can just win games and it’s all about winning games’. And I absolutely get that when it comes to management.

“Of course, it’s about results, very much, it’s a results-driven business. But I was given this job to get us out of bother last year.

“And we came in, the first thing wasn’t about, yes, results were important, but it was making sure that the team were capable and prepared to go and get those results.

“I think we are prepared to go and get those results. We just haven’t given our support enough good days to celebrate wins.

“But the work doesn’t stop. And it doesn’t deter me one bit from the work that I do on the training field.

“I’ll hopefully see a team flourish, get the results that I think their performances deserve. And then we can all come together with the unity that we showed last season and hopefully Kilmarnock will start climbing the table.”

#2207. De Laurentiis: “In casa Napoli non esiste nessun caso”

La decisione del presidente Aurelio De Laurentiis di blindare la squadra in ritiro cancella l'incontro con la stampa prima del match contro la Lazio.

A pochi minuti dall'inizio previsto per le 15:00, con i giornalisti già presenti a Castel Volturno, la conferenza di Massimiliano Allegri in vista del match contro la Lazio è stata annullata. Il Napoli ha motivato la scelta con la decisione di blindare la squadra in ritiro ed evitare distrazioni mediatiche prima della sfida di domani.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

In casa Napoli non esiste nessun caso. Quando mi sono accorto che stavamo per fare l’ennesima conferenza ho preferito bloccarla. Perché? Perché non credo che le conferenze stampa servano prima delle partite, considerando che giochiamo ogni tre giorni. Siamo in ritiro e bisogna evitare qualunque distrazione per i calciatori dalla loro concentrazione alla partita. Quando si va in ritiro la tutela di tutti deve essere totale. Aurelio De Laurentiis.

#2206. Derby County need to target winter swoop for 25-year-old after Blackburn Rovers summer interest: Opinion

Derby County are in the Championship relegation zone and have struggled for points. DCFC will get the chance to bolster their squad when the January transfer window opens up for business.

Dundee United left-back Will Ferry was heavily linked with a move to Blackburn Rovers in the summer. However, nothing materialised on that front in the end and he remained in Scotland beyond the deadline in September.

The Rams should now turn their attention to the defender and try and lure him to Pride Park this winter. Ferry, 25, is out of contract at the end of the season and his current club risk losing him for free in June 2027 if they don’t sell him in January, assuming he doesn’t pen an extension anytime soon.

The Bury-born man has made 91 appearances for Dundee United in all competitions to date, eight of which have come in this campaign, and he has chipped in with five goals and an eye-catching 15 assists from the back. He has a nice left foot and should move back down to England soon for a new challenge in his career.

Derby County currently have Craig Forsyth and Derry Murkin in the treatment room. Therefore, DCFC could do with another option in their position on the left flank of defence.

The Rams have had to play the likes of Ryan Hedges and Ryan Nyambe there over recent times. Ferry would be ideal for them now and could plug a gap for the time being.

The Republic of Ireland international, who has one cap to his name, has proved himself up in Scotland. He likes to put crosses into the box as much as possible and attacking players like Carlton Morris and Patrick Agyemang (when he’s fit) will benefit from his delivery.

Ferry rose up through Southampton’s academy before he was loaned out to Crawley Town as a youngster to get some experience under his belt. He then had two permanent years at Cheltenham Town before Dundee United came calling for his services.

Dundee United will want to receive a fee of some sort for Ferry and not lose him for nothing next year. Derby County should try and test their resolve.

The Rams can’t afford to get their recruitment wrong in January and need the right type of characters. At 25, Ferry’s next move is a big one and he needs to go somewhere he is guaranteed regular minutes.

Up next for Derby County is a clash away against Ferry’s old team Southampton after the international break. The Saints are eyeing promotion to the Premier League under Tonda Eckert.

#2204. Ex-Celtic star tells Martin O'Neill why he's on receiving end of 'flak with love'

Joe Hart has told Martin O'Neill why he is getting "flak with love" amid Celtic's stuttering form.

Scrutiny at the club is growing and growing after a draw with Dundee United was followed up by defeat to Falkirk. Previously, the domestic form had been almost flawless, but for losing to Rangers.

Fans are now concerned their lead at the top of the table is precarious and are questioning the direction of the club even more.

Former Parkhead goalkeeper Hart says that scrutiny is always going to be there and it does not affect O'Neill's standing with the support.

He told The Overlap: "It’s flak with love, and that doesn’t make any sense. Of course, we know it doesn’t make any sense, but Martin O’Neill will be, and is, absolutely adored. But he knows what he signed up for as a Celtic manager, and he would expect to be getting a lot of questions asked about him.

Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

And that’s not saying he’s not up to the task or he’s not the man for the job, but that’s what comes with the territory. If you really understand Celtic, you understand that if you’re not borderline perfect domestically and challenging in Europe, you’re going to get it.

"You’re going to get it because they care and they’re intelligent football fans. And, there’s a massive disharmony with the board. The fans really don’t understand what the direction of the club is. And obviously the board have got their opinions in terms of the success that they had and continue to have.

So, it is difficult. That was really shining brightly mid-season last season, but then Martin came back in and the team started to win and it goes away. It’s amazing what winning can do, and at the moment they’re not.

"They had a difficult result at Falkirk. I think they drew at home to Dundee United. And then this Besiktas game felt ominous. It felt like there was going to be a riot, or not even a riot. Do you know what the worst feeling you can have in a stadium is? And I very rarely felt it up there. It wasn’t anger, it was people going, ‘Pfft, we lost again.’ That is the worst feeling you could have.

"You’d rather have someone that impassioned, that embroiled as a Celtic fan. Like I say, domestically, I lost very, very few games, but no matter what run you’d been on, you could feel it. It wasn’t the majority, but you’d feel some people’s whole life and whole livelihood is proudly Celtic.

"And if you don’t perform in that shirt, you’re going to get it. I’ve still got friends up there, and they were flat going into the game. If Celtic had lost, they wouldn’t have been angry, they’d have been like, ‘Oh, God.’ And that’s not a nice feeling. I talked about it for Michael [Carrick], but I think it’s a little bit different up there, because they’re still top of the league.

"If they can take the atmosphere that they generated towards the end of the game last night into the league game this weekend, I think it’s Kilmarnock, then it could be a massive spark to go again.”

#2202. 3 players who Birmingham City should offload in January, including Lee Buchanan

Birmingham City have enjoyed a fine season to date after a slightly different approach in the summer transfer window. BCFC made seven new signings, two of whom had already been at the club, so it was a window of evolution not revolution as opposed to previous squad rebuilds.

But, with Chris Davies‘ side firmly in the Championship promotion conversation, the January window offers a chance to strengthen. The Blues can shift out some fringe players to make way for additions who can push them over the line in the bid to make the Premier League.

With that in mind, we put forward three players who should be leaving Birmingham City in the winter…

Somewhat surprisingly, Scottish winger Scott Wright stayed at St Andrew’s in the summer. The 29-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Dundee and the strong competition for minutes on the Birmingham City wings meant minutes were bound to be limited.

That has proven to be the case with Wright making only two Championship matchday squads and playing just one minute of senior football in a brief substitute appearance against Swansea City in the Carabao Cup.

Wright sees his contract expire in 2027, but to get back to playing regularly, he should leave BCFC in the winter. A return to Scotland or drop to League One seem like his most likely options.

Another player who has been on the fringes at Birmingham City is Lee Buchanan, although his situation is a little different. There was talk of a potential summer loan move as the left-back rebuilt his fitness after a serious knee injury, but he ended up staying put.

Alex Cochrane‘s emergence in the starting XI and the signing of Kristoffer Lund have left Buchanan as third choice in his favoured position. The Blues have been eager to be careful with his minutes given how long he was out, but by the time January comes around, he should be ready to play more regualrly.

There may be hesitance to cash in right away, so a loan feels more likely for January. Then, his situation can be reassessed in the summer, as he has shown he can be a Championship option before.

Last but not least is Marvin Ducksch, who has made eight Championship appearances off the bench. The German striker showed signs of promise in his debut campaign at Birmingham City, but a drink driving charge brought doubts over his future.

A summer move failed to materialise, but it is still widely expected that the 32-year-old moves on this season. A switch back to Germany is most likely, and could see Ducksch return to impressive form given his record of 71 goals in 138 2. Bundesliga appearances, and 34 in 130 in the Bundesliga.

August Priske is the lead striker at BCFC with Jay Stansfield and Luis Vasquez as the other options. Another centre forward may be needed if Ducksch is sold, but that seems like a logical switch.

#2201. Mika Baur identifies the Celtic challenge he is ready to rise to

Mika Baur is enjoying the demands of being a Celtic player – and was delighted to see the team display their fighting spirit and belief as they broke their Europa League duck.

The 22-year-old impressed as Celtic came from behind to beat Besiktas 3-2 on Thursday and get off the mark in the Europa League at the fourth time of asking.

The Hoops were heading for a seventh defeat in 11 matches when they fell behind early in the second half but the introduction of Callum Osmand, Camilo Duran and Colby Donovan on the hour mark sparked the team into life.

Manager Martin O’Neill recently admitted that some new players were still adapting to the demands of playing for Celtic but Baur and Duran have quickly proved they were successful summer signings.

Baur arrived from Paderborn after helping them to promotion to the Bundesliga and made his Germany debut last month, but moving to Scotland has been a new experience.

Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

“To play every three days is different for me,” the midfielder said. “I think I have played the same amount of games now that I had last season by the winter break.

“But I like it. That’s what you want. You want to play all the time, more playing than training. I am really enjoying it.

“And I think the pressure to win is a good kind of pressure. It’s better than (trying) not to lose. So I really enjoy it.”

Baur has shown pace and skill on the ball but his pressing in the final stages drew massive appreciation from the crowd on Thursday.

“First of all, I want to work hard for the team, for myself, that I can prove myself and I can play on the stage, help the team, put in a shift, hard work,” he said.

“That’s what I have to do first. And then after this, the skill comes, playing with the ball. But first of all, it’s showing heart on the field. I was really happy that it was appreciated.”

The win over the Turkish side felt like it could be a major step in Celtic’s season as they bounced back from losing the opening goal and from a late equaliser, with Duran netting the winner seconds later.

“The second half was pure heart, pure fight,” Baur said. “I’m not here for a long time, but I think that’s what it’s all about. This win feels unbelievable because we deserved it. We fought for it.

“The team is really, really close together. We know that we had a tough couple of weeks, but you can feel it in the training sessions, how the team is working together, the feeling, the believing is always there. And it was there on the pitch. That’s what we have to show week by week, every three days.

“It was not just our win. The atmosphere was great. I’m really, really thankful for every supporter in the stadium. They gave us a lot of energy. We all fight together. That makes me happy.”

#2200. It pushes you forward – Jacob Murrell feeling fuelled by Falkirk fan fervour

Falkirk striker Jacob Murrell believes the passion of Scottish football is fuelling his goalscoring form.

The American has netted five goals since joining from DC United, helping the Bairns go on a four-game winning run ahead of Sunday’s trip to face Hearts.

The 22-year-old said: “It’s a little different just because the games matter a bit more here than they did back in the MLS, just because of the promotion/relegation and how much the fans care about results. So the intensity of the games is much higher, you’re not finding easy games.

“For me, it’s the best thing in the world to play under this type of pressure. It just gives me a purpose, it gives me that fuel.

“I love that aspect of it. I love that the way that our group goes on the field and performs matters to people. That’s the most special thing about what we get to do and it drives us on the hard days when we have to come to training, when we’re tired, when we’re sore.

Mika Baur identifies the Celtic challenge he is ready to rise to Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team

"We’re playing for something more than ourselves, that pushes you forward.

“Like after the Celtic match, when all the fans stayed in their seats, celebrated the win with us after, that wasn’t just a win for us as a team, but for the full club, for the fans, for the community. It was a really great moment for everybody.”

Murrell was among 17 summer signings but manager John McGlynn has quickly fashioned the group into an effective team.

“The people have been really good to me,” he said. “Falkirk in general has been really good to me. The club, the team-mates, but then the fans as well have been really good.

“There’s a bit of learning curve the first month to get up to speed and get all the stuff sorted with a car, an apartment and a bank account. All the stuff that you don’t see behind the scenes.

“Little stuff that’s different, like when I went to the grocery store, I couldn’t find eggs. Back home, they’re only in the fridge. They’re on the shelf here.

“But I’ve got into a really good rhythm with a couple of team-mates going to the gym after training and just getting into good habits where we’re cooking our own food and eating well.

“Just feeling full of confidence that we’re putting in the work and we’re going to reap the benefits of it.”

#2199. Data estimates how much Sheffield United star Sydie Peck is worth as midweek hattrick continues excellent start to the season

Sheffield United continued their impressive run of form on Tuesday night, securing a 3-2 victory away at Preston North End. SUFC are now unbeaten in four matches and have won four of their last six Championship outings.

It was an impressive all-round team display, but Sydie Peck was undoubtedly the standout performer. The 22-year-old midfielder produced a superb hat-trick in a man-of-the-match performance, becoming the first Sheffield United player to score a competitive first-team hat-trick since Billy Sharp against Aston Villa in February 2019.

Peck’s display was another reminder of his growing importance to the Blades, having also been the subject of recent exit speculation. The midfielder was linked with a move to now fellow Championship side West Ham over the summer.

Peck arrived at Bramall Lane from Arsenal’s academy as a free agent in 2021 and has made 105 appearances for the first team after a brief National League loan at Oldham Athletic.

SUFC will likely not allow Peck to go for a small fee, with a fee of £15m as a baseline the likely ball-park. Whether sides keen on the England U21 midfielder would value him at that is unknown.

FootballTransfers.com’s Estimated Transfer Value (ETV) model places him at €16.2 million (approximately £13.5m at current rates), with a range of €14.6m–€17.8m. This sits above the current FootballTransfers valuation of Divine Mukasa (around €12.8m) and is higher than most Championship players of a similar age-range.

Peck’s age as well as his status as an England youth international will see his value be higher than some other Championship midfielders.

Peck made his senior breakthrough during the 2024/25 campaign before taking another significant step forward last season, registering five goals and five assists in 41 appearances across all competitions.

The London-born midfielder attracted interest during the summer, but he made clear his desire to repay those who have shown faith in him at Bramall Lane, including manager Chris Wilder.

Peck remains happy at Sheffield United, and his performances this season suggest staying put has done little to slow his development. However, if he maintains his current level, further interest is inevitable, potentially making a move away increasingly difficult to turn down.

Sheffield United are keen to secure a new contract for Peck, with his existing agreement due to expire in 2028. The Blades would be wise to act sooner rather than later, with his recent displays likely to attract plenty of attention from elsewhere.

#2198. 3 midfielders Blackburn Rovers should target in January after Mowbray admission, including 2018/19 loan star

Blackburn Rovers only signed three players in the summer transfer window, and sights are already set on January targets. Tony Mowbray has voiced a need to bolster in central midfield, with Adam Forshaw’s absence leaving only Kristi Montgomery, Sam Morsy, Moussa Baradji and Jake Garrett to pick from.

Rovers aren’t flush for cash, so they will likely have to be shrewd in their winter business. A lack of experience in the absences of Morsy and Forshaw mean some extra pedigree would be welcomed too.

Here, we put forward three options for the recruitment team at Ewood Park to consider…

First up is someone who would be a highly popular signing at Blackburn Rovers. Midfielder Harrison Reed spent a highly successful loan spell at Ewood Park in the 2018/19 season, providing three goals and seven assists in 36 games while away from former club Southampton.

He would join Fulham off the back of his Rovers stay, and he has played 212 times for the club since. However, Reed is down the pecking order under Alvaro Arbeloa having failed to make a Premier League matchday squad since August, despite being fit and available.

A drop to the Championship would give him the game time he deserves. Reed would bring experience, leadership and a well-rounded skillset to Tony Mowbray’s side and would be a very impressive addition.

A player in a similar position to Reed is Alan Browne, who has bags of Championship experience to his name but is currently struggling for minutes in the Premier League with Sunderland. The Irishman has only played in cup competitions and it seems highly unlikely that he makes a resurgence at the Stadium of Light.

Browne has been a player of interest to Blackburn Rovers before, and his vast second tier experience would make him an influential player on and off the pitch. The 31-year-old would bring leadership in the dressing room, offering an energetic box-to-box presence in midfield.

This paired with a strong technical game and versatility made Browne a regular in Middlesbrough’s push for the Championship play-offs while on loan last season.

Last but not least is a more left-field option, but Julius Magnusson would be a great player for Blackburn Rovers and potentially a real hit in the Championship. The 28-year-old Iceland international is a key man for Swedish side Elfsborg, and he has stood out over their 2026 season.

Magnusson is a very well-rounded player, chipping in with six goals and three assists in 30 games across all competitions this year, as per Fotmob. Amongst Allsvenskan midfielders, he ranks amongst the best in defensive contributions (200 – top 1%), interceptions (53 – top 3%), aerial duels won (55 – top 1%), line-breaking passes (217 – top 13%) and touches (1,659 – top 8%).

Those stats reflect his wide skillset, and at his age, he likely wouldn’t break the bank. Magnusson could come in and be a real hit for Rovers if they are happy to pay a fee to pry him out of his contract until 2029.

#2197. Turki Alalshikh blame rejected as Derby County crisis deepens

It has been a nightmare start to the season for Derby County in the Championship.

After missing out on the play-offs on the final day of last season, Derby would have been hoping to challenge for promotion once again this campaign, but John Eustace's men currently find themselves at the wrong end of the table.

Derby owner David Clowes has made no secret of his desire to bring fresh investment into the club in recent years, and it looked as though a cash injection was imminent after Saudi billionaire Turki Alalshikh agreed to purchase a controlling stake in the club.

The proposed deal had been given approval by the EFL and the Independent Football Regulator, but Alalshikh unexpectedly withdrew from the takeover in August, claiming that, as the campaign had already started, he had "no time to prepare the team or the club for the season ahead".

While the Rams went on to make further signings after Alalshikh's takeover deal collapsed, including the permanent addition of midfielder David Ozoh for a fee of around £4 million, head coach John Eustace later claimed that the saga caused the club to lose "a lot of momentum on players that we were looking at".

After the off-field drama over the summer, Derby have made a disastrous start to the season on the pitch, and they head into the November international break sitting in the Championship relegation zone, with pressure building on Eustace as increasing numbers of supporters call for a managerial change.

When asked if Alalshikh's takeover falling through at the last minute is to blame for the club's poor start, FLW's Derby County fan pundit Shaun Woodward admitted that it is a contributing factor, as well as the recent injury crisis, but he insisted that a managerial change is the only way to get the Rams out of their current predicament.

"There is definitely an element of blame on Turki Alalshikh for pulling out so late in the day, but we can't be pinning it all on the takeover," Shaun told FLW.

"John Eustace still has a more than capable squad at his disposal.

"The majority of that squad was good enough to get us to an eighth-placed finish last season.

"Yes, it might have affected the transfers he had pencilled in, and we had to then go for plan B or plan C transfers, but the nucleus of that squad is still far too good to be in the position that we find ourselves in now.

"Yes, you can also blame injuries to our backline, but, again, the players that have stepped in should be doing better, they are still Championship players.

"They are not covering themselves in any glory whatsoever, and you can say the same about Eustace and his staff because they haven't been able to motivate the players, their tactics seem wrong, he doesn't sound very inspiring in his post-match interviews, and he looks defeated.

"The players look lost out on the pitch, but, all of that said, you can blame Eustace as much as you want, and he will lose his job because of this as the buck stops with him, the players have let him down massively as well.

"The last couple of performances especially at Millwall and at home to Norwich, the players have downed tools, they have given up.

"They are very much playing in individual mode, where they don't want to be made the scapegoat, they are hiding on the pitch, we can all see it as fans.

"No one is looking like they really care, and it's sad to see because there's still a nucleus of players out on that pitch that should be far better than 23rd in the league with the lowest goals scored and the highest goals conceded.

"We're not creating anything, we're gifting teams goal after goal, so I think there's an element of everything involved here.

"Yes, the takeover didn't help, maybe the transfers weren't the ones we wanted necessarily, but I still felt we had a good enough squad.

"Injuries haven't helped the backline, but the players that have come in haven't stepped up, and the more experienced players in our squad haven't led by example.

"It's just been a shambles, and, let's be real, the warning signs were there in pre-season, we looked lathargic and unfit, and that's carried on into the season.

"Until we get a new manager, I just can't see it changing, and, even then, it's going to be tough for someone to come in with the current group.

"The confidence is rock bottom, someone is going to have to come in and change formation, change personnel, rip up the script and start again because right now, we're only heading one way and that's League One."

While Alalshikh agreed a deal to invest in Derby and went through the EFL and IFR approval processes, Clowes and Eustace must have known that there was always a chance his takeover could collapse, particularly given that his previous interest in other Championship clubs, such as Bristol City and Millwall, had failed to progress.

Alalshikh's late withdrawal would inevitably have caused some disruption to the Rams' transfer plans, but Eustace still has a competitive squad at his disposal, which includes many of those who helped the club to an eighth-placed finish last season.

Can Turki Alalshikh's failed takeover be blamed for Derby County's poor start? Tell us in the comments below!

With that in mind, there is little excuse for Derby to be in their current position, even taking their extensive injury list into account, and it is difficult not to feel that Eustace will be fortunate to survive the upcoming international break.

#2196. Marink Reedijk lays down Aberdeen challenge to Hibs team after Hearts win

Hibernian manager Marink Reedijk has challenged his players to replicate their Hampden hunger against Aberdeen as they get back in the “rat race”.

Reedijk told his players “I want music, I want beer, I want everything” when they returned to the dressing room after beating Hearts in the Premier Sport Cup semi-finals and joined in a rendition of Sunshine on Leith with their fans.

But the Dutchman is now determined to secure a first William Hill Premiership win when Hibs travel to Pittodrie.

“It was a very beautiful moment,” he said. “After the match, you saw what it meant to the fans, what it meant to the club and what it meant to the players. That is important because this is what football is about.

“The best thing for me was that we showed we can get a result in the way we want to play. We can come back from 1-0 down, play beautiful football but also do the dirty work. That was important to see.

It pushes you forward – Jacob Murrell feeling fuelled by Falkirk fan fervour Mika Baur identifies the Celtic challenge he is ready to rise to

“However, it’s history now. We need to make sure we can do it over multiple matches and for a longer period of time.

“If you achieve something as we did on Sunday, it’s important to celebrate it. We work hard, so you can also party for an evening. Then, from that point, we need to focus on Aberdeen.

“We’re in a sort of rat race, with game after game after game. We do everything at the highest possible intensity, from training sessions to matches. Therefore, you need to celebrate your victories sometimes.”

He added: “For me, it’s important that we make another step in the way we want to play. We need to do things better than we did in the last match. Whether it’s Hearts or someone else, we need to have the same hunger for every match.”

After scoring during Everton's 3-1 victory over Coventry City on Friday night, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall sent a message to Leicester City supporters on social media.

The midfielder left Leicester City to join Chelsea in 2024, but departed for Everton just a year later. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall has since become something of a fan favourite on Merseyside and is enjoying yet another solid campaign so far.

His former side were playing in the FA Cup on Friday night, winning 4-2 against Oxford City while the Premier League saw Everton host Coventry City. The contrast was stark but Dewsbury-Hall made his feelings known immediately after the goal.

During the 2023/24 season, Dewsbury-Hall picked up 27 goal involvements to help Enzo Maresca's Leicester make an immediate return to the top flight. That included a brace against Coventry on the opening day of the season.

He also scored a third goal against them during a 3-1 defeat in the reverse fixture, meanig three of his 12 goals that season were bagged against Leicester's midlands rivals.

Dewsbury'-Hall smashed home the third of a 3-1 win against Frank Lampard's Coventry last night, with the 28-year-old not holding back during his celebration whatsoever. He stuck his tongue out and pointed to the badge before kissing it against his old nemesis.

#2194. Data estimates how much Cardiff City star Jack Moylan is worth ahead of potential January interest

Cardiff City have made a respectable start to life back in the Championship, although Brian Barry-Murphy’s side have struggled to find consistency in front of goal. Their problems in the final third have arguably left them lower down the table than their overall performances deserve.

However, those struggles have not affected summer recruit Jack Moylan. The Bluebirds decision to bring the attacking midfielder in from Lincoln City is already looking like an excellent piece of business.

The 25-year-old has quickly established himself as one of the Bluebirds’ most influential players, registering nine goals and three assists in his opening 14 Championship appearances. Moylan has also started every league fixture, highlighting just how important he has become to Barry-Murphy’s plans.

With Cardiff struggling towards the lower end of the table, his contributions have been particularly valuable. If he continues producing at this level, the Bluebirds may have to contend with growing interest in their summer signing when the January transfer window opens.

While the fee was reported as undisclosed upon Moylan’s announcement, reports have suggested that Cardiff City was an initial £3m which could rise to £5m.

The Bluebirds have tied Moylan down to a four-year deal running until the summer of 2028. With that in mind, if interest does arrive in January, they are in a strong position to ask for a hefty fee and profit.

However, the data suggests that Cardiff City may have overpaid to bring Moylan in this summer, which does not bode well for a potential sale. FootballTransfers’ estimated transfer value has the attacking-midfielder’s value at €2.2m, which is around £1.8m.

Off the current Cardiff City squad, Moylan has the second highest value with only Yousef Salech higher (€3.8m). Moylan’s value is also considerably lower than the only player who has more Championship goals then him Will Lankshear, who is valued at €20.7m.

A more direct comparison may be Blackburn Rovers striker Andri Gudjohnsen, who also has nine goals this campaign. His value is only €2.7m and much similar to Moylan’s, while being just a year younger.

Moylan’s statistics underline just how influential he has become for Cardiff City. His attacking numbers are particularly impressive, with 51 shots, 19 on target and 18 chances created.

He has also registered five big chances created, while his nine goals have come from an expected goals figure of 5.48, highlighting his clinical finishing and ability to outperform the underlying numbers.

The Irishman has delivered in some of Cardiff’s biggest performances, scoring twice in their 5-1 victory over Watford while impressing in a central striking role. He also scored a first-half hat-trick in the 3-3 draw with West Ham during the week.

Having progressed from Irish football to becoming a key figure in Lincoln’s League One title-winning campaign, Moylan has adapted impressively to the Championship.

#2193. ‘Upset’ - Ryan Alebiosu sends message to Blackburn Rovers fans after suffering new blow

Blackburn Rovers star Ryan Alebiosu has seemingly confirmed that he will not be available for selection again until 2027.

The athletic right-back limped off during the first half of Rovers' 2-1 loss to Stoke City in midweek, as he managed just 40 minutes before being forced out of the game with an issue.

The 24-year-old has been a key figure for the Lancashire outfit so far this campaign, featuring in all of their opening 14 league matches.

So his absence will come as a big blow for Tony Mowbray, who will have to handle missing one of their top stars for the remainder of the calendar year.

Summer signing Gady Beyuku was brought on to replace Alebiosu late in the first half, with the team going 1-0 down just a few moments later, with the Potters sealing all three points in the second half.

Alebiosu has confirmed on his Instagram page that he will be absent for the remainder of 2026, ruling him out for a number of weeks with an issue.

The defender was initially a doubt for this weekend’s clash against West Ham, with Mowbray hopeful he could be available, but a further scan has revealed a more significant issue than first feared.

“Gutted, upset but god has bigger plans,” wrote Alebiosu.

“Will be back stronger for sure, see you 2027 Rovers.”

Alebiosu also missed a period of games for Blackburn last season due to the Africa Cup of Nations, but his absence will still be a big blow for the team.

The defender has previously been linked with the likes of Everton off the back of his performances at Ewood Park, following a 2025 move from Belgian outfit Kortrijk.

This injury also means he will miss the upcoming Lancashire derby against bitter rivals Burnley, which will be a particularly painful pill for Mowbray to swallow.

No exact timeframe has been given for his potential return beyond 2027, meaning he will be absent for at least eight weeks.

Alebiosu had started each of Rovers’ first 14 league fixtures, and he’s been one of the standout performers under Mowbray so far this term.

The full-back has impressed going forward, completing 0.85 dribbles per 90, and getting 1.85 touches in the opposition area each game on average (all stats from Fotmob).

He contributed one goal and five assists from 39 appearances in the Championship last season, highlighting his attacking threat, although he is yet to register either a goal or assist in 2026/27.

Alebiosu’s absence is a massive blow for Mowbray, as he has become a very dependable performer for the club.

And with a more inexperienced figure in Beyuku coming in for the Nigerian - one who hasn't necessarily impressed in his cameos so far - there may be some short-term pain at Ewood Park whilst the French defender gets to grips with the Championship.

An injury of around eight weeks means that the experienced coach will have to get creative to deal with this particular injury issue.

#2192. Celtic's 'Che Guevaras' should show their fellow fans some respect at this year's AGM

There is about as much chance of Dermot Desmond taking a seat amongst the Union Bears ultras group the next time Celtic play Rangers at Ibrox in January as there is of the billionaire Irish financier rocking up at their AGM at Parkhead next month.

Desmond, who has been the Glasgow club’s principal shareholder for more than two decades, has not attended the gathering since way back in 2006 and he is not, with disaffection about the stewardship of the Scottish champions still rife in the stands, about to break with tradition.

The greeting which chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay, interim chairman Brian Wilson and manager Martin O’Neill received from some protesters when they attended a question-and-answer session at the Greenock Supporters’ Club this week gave an indication of the sort of treatment he would receive if he did.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of the Europa League encounter with Besiktas on Thursday night, O’Neill expressed his dismay at the fact that around 25 supporters appeared wearing face coverings. “That was the saddest thing,” he said. “I would never have thought that fans would be clothed in balaclavas at a meeting.”

The frustration in the statement which the Celtic Fans Collective, an umbrella coalition of supporters’ clubs and organisations, published this week demanding that Desmond make a rare appearance at the meeting was palpable and understandable.

That the man who, rightly or wrongly but unquestionably, wields the most power at Parkhead is an annual no-show highlights everything that is wrong with how the former European Cup winners are being run. Are accountability and dialogue too much to ask for?

Is the famously publicity-shy man from Macroom in County Cork, though, really going to trap when the same individuals who hurled tennis balls at him when he was playing golf in the Alfred Dunhill Championship at St Andrews last month are likely to be in attendance?

There has been fevered speculation about when Celtic directors will face their shareholders in recent weeks. Supporters are desperate to know what their long-term football strategy is, who has been driving recruitment, how governance is going to be modernised, why tens of millions of pounds continue to sit in the bank and much else besides.

But are they likely to get answers to those questions now the AGM date has been set for Tuesday, December 1? The actions of a certain sub-section of their support in Inverclyde in midweek suggested that it could well be another bad-tempered, ugly and ultimately futile get-together.

Celtic interim chairman Brian Wilson, left, chief executive Michael Nicholson and chief financial officer Chris McKay at Parkhead (Image: Stuart Wallace / Shutterstock)

Ill-feeling about then-chairman Peter Lawwell bringing last year's annual meeting to a premature end amid persistent disorder still lingers. It has been suggested once again in recent days that the move was a cynical ploy by the besieged board to avoid public scrutiny.

However, David Low, the financial analyst who was a driving force behind the Fergus McCann takeover back in 1994 and is now associated with the Celtic Supporters Limited pressure group, rejected that interpretation of events when he appeared on the A Celtic State of Mind podcast last week.

“You are allowed to hold the people who shareholders elected to account once a year,” he said. “But it is a professional environment. Last year’s meeting was a bun fight. Nobody came out of that looking well. It is a professional forum and you have to respect the forum you are in.

“Give them red cards if you have to if they give an unsatisfactory answer. But listen to what is said and then react. That is the way it has always been at Celtic, even when it was a private company.

“That was a horrible meeting last year. People go there who want to learn. That is why they are there. You turn up, you ask questions and you try to learn something. If you don’t like it you can boo and do whatever within reason. But you have got to listen.

“It disintegrated into a shambles last year. It was over-the-top. There was a lot of unacceptable behaviour from the hardcore. It was not on. It was the biggest AGM in 20 years.”

There has been widespread unhappiness about the course Celtic are on for some time and a substantial section of the support wants meaningful change in how the Parkhead club is run. But some of the more vocal and militant members of the rebel alliance can be arrogant and selfish.

They did not merely show disrespect to the board last year. They showed disrespect to the hundreds of fellow shareholders who had turned up, many from far afield, wanting to exercise the same right to scrutinise those running their club.

The club later alleged that its head of safety, security and operations, Mark Hargreaves, had been threatened and intimidated by two prominent members of the Green Brigade. Whatever the truth of those allegations, it was a sorry affair from start to premature finish.

Celtic fans hold up banners referencing their teams failures against teams in Europe (Image: Andrew Milligan)

One lifelong fan voiced his exasperation at the leaders of the civil war that was raging at his beloved club in these pages as he attended the Scottish Gas Scottish Cup game against Dundee back in February.

“We don't need modern-day Che Guevaras,” he said before he ignored the boycott that had been called. “We want people who love Celtic.” He is not alone in taking that view.

The Celtic Fans Collective appealed for the “focus to be firmly on scrutiny rather than protest” at the AGM in their latest missive. They are right. The board should be made to answer searching questions. Those who shout directors down before their answers can be heard are serving neither their cause nor their fellow supporters.

It would perhaps help the Parkhead club to move forward on and off the park if those words were heeded and there were no disruptions from “aggressive and irrational factions” hellbent on “stirring up toxicity”.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Shane Duffy made his Derby County debut against Bolton Wanderers, with the Rams winning just their second league game of the season to ease their relegation fears somewhat.

The Championship relegation picture was looking bleak for Derby County if they had lost to Bolton Wanderers, but their second half fightback claimed a massive three points for John Eustace and co.

Shane Duffy played the full 90 minutes after sitting on the bench during the two previous games, with the Irishman making his 220th Championship appearance against Bolton. He was 1-0 down at half-time but they sealed a 3-1 win late in the match.

Duffy reacted to the win during his debut for the club on Instagram, saying: "We’re back 🐏"

Among the replies was Dion Sanderson, adding: "Just got duffied 👅👅👅"

Derby midfielder David Ozoh also said: "😍"

Bobby Clark was also quick to respond, stating: "❤️"

Duffy's former Yeovil Town teammate Luke Ayling also replied: "Love it big fella!"

Duffy has built an impressive career across English football, coming through Everton's academy before spells with Blackburn Rovers and Brighton, where he helped the Seagulls secure promotion to the Premier League.

He also enjoyed a spell at Celtic before spending three seasons with Norwich City, making 87 appearances for the Canaries. Now united with Eustace at Derby on an initial two-month deal, the 34-year-old brings considerable and vital experience at a perilous time at Pride Park.

#2189. Manchester United player ratings: United failed to win despite advantage

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

Substitutions by Michael Carrick around the hour mark made the difference as United showed intent before Mbeumo got the goal off Cunha’s low cross. Luke Shaw was at the end of a scuffle with Bentancur, who was shown a red card for headbutting Shaw.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

Lenne Sammens-6          Quiet afternoon for United no.1 till the goal, where he saw the ball go into the back of the net.

Leny Yoro-6       Defensively was fine but offered little upfront. Played out of position, and he showed good defensive awareness on the right back till his substitution.

Kobbie Mainoo-6.5        Brilliant defensive tackle to deny Tottenham in the 68th minute. Remained composed in tight spaces against a physical Tottenham midfield.

Youri Tielemans-6          A decent performance and was solid throughout the minutes he was on the field

Bruno Fernandes-5        Another quiet and disappointing evening for the United captain after he failed to impress on a day he needed to get a result for United.

Amad-6              A positive return from injury, showed plenty of promise on the wing but failed to get past a resolute Tottenham side

Matheus Cunha-7           One of the liveliest options for United going forward. Provided an assist to Mbeumo to put United up front

Bryan Mbeumo-7.5        A brilliant finish off Matheus Cunha’s low ball to put United in front. Was dangerous going forward and denied a second on a counter by Kinsky off a brilliant long ball by Baleba.

#2188. 19-year-old Southampton starlet showcasing exciting potential in European loan after early transfer interest

Southampton sent eight players out on loan this campaign. With a mixture of academy talents and players who are on their way out of St Mary’s, the Saints are seeing mixed success from the departed members of the squad.

Moses Sesay, Nicholas Oyekunle and Jay Robinson were the three teenagers to leave for the season. It’s the latter who Tonda Eckert will be monitoring closely after a breakout term last year in the Championship.

Robinson made 28 appearances for Southampton, scoring twice and providing an assist. Minutes were always going to be hard to come by for the 19-year-old this season. With a move to Monza secured, the attacker has plenty to prove in the Serie A.

Securing a loan move to Serie A is a positive sign of how much potential Robinson has to unlock. It’s safe to say that despite a slow start to life at Monza, the 19-year-old is becoming a key player for the Italian outfit.

The Southampton academy graduate had to wait until September to make his first start, and he impressed in a 1-0 win against Torino. Featuring in an attacking midfield role, he completed the most dribbles in the game with four and had nine touches inside the opposition’s box.

His first goal came in the next match, in which he completed 78% of his passes and was dispossessed only once. Former Saints boss Ivan Juric has shown full faith in Robinson, starting the teenager in three of the last four outings.

The 19-year-old’s best display came against Cagliari, where he scored once in a 4-0 win. Two out of his three dribbles were successful in the game, and he made three line-breaking passes. It has been an impressive loan stint for the youngster with Inter Milan registering their interest.

Southampton have the option to recall Robinson from his loan spell in January. However, given his promising spell so far, the Saints would be reckless to do so.

At left-wing, the South Coast outfit currently have the options of Leo Scienza and Sam Edozie, as well as Lewis Dobbin, who can play there too. Edozie is likely to depart in January, though, after putting in a transfer request late in the summer window.

This would ultimately leave Eckert’s side short of attackers in that position. However, they must avoid recalling Robinson to improve their depth. Even if Edozie were to leave, his exit would give Dobbin a better chance of breaking into the first team after just 409 minutes played.

Most importantly, it would do no favours to the 19-year-old’s development. The Southampton prospect has only recently become settled at Monza, and with his minutes increasing over the last couple of months, the South Coast outfit can’t afford to ruin his crucial playing time.

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

#2186. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2185. The Celtic 'rollercoaster' Mika Baur is getting used to & how he spends his days off

It is easy to forget that Mika Baur only turned 22 over the summer. The German midfielder displayed maturity beyond his years in Celtic's captivating Europa League victory over Besiktas on Thursday evening, chasing lost causes, contributing defensively, and progressing play forward when the opportunity arrived.

It was his finest performance since joining the club for an initial fee of £4.5 million from Paderborn in August.

Baur compared his first few months in Glasgow to riding a rollercoaster, with downtime away from the football pitch proving rare.

"There’s no time to think about it! We are playing every three days and I really try to fight and bring my heart on the field all the time," Baur said. "Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t, but I hope people understand as a young player it can be tough to be comfortable in a new country, a new culture and new club.

"But I really try my best. I have felt good in my first few months but it is a bit of a rollercoaster.

"Playing in this unbelievable stadium in front of these fans, getting the call-up to the national team was a big honour. You feel the pressure with some of the games we have lost but I am getting used to it."

This is Baur's first time living away from home. He credits his partner for making the transition to Scotland smoother, even if chances to play some golf are limited.

"I’m grateful to my girlfriend as she does most things and makes it comfortable at home," Baur continued. "The club also have people who have helped us a lot to settle.

"But you don’t get much time – you get home and lie on the couch!

"It’s not all stressful though. It’s also nice to go somewhere new and learn the city, get to coffee shops and restaurants.

"We’ve been to the beach, we’ve been to Edinburgh, we try to see a lot on our day off.

"I also play golf – so I’ve come to the home of golf! I’ve only managed to get to the driving range though. When you are playing every three days it’s a bit much to play nine or 18 holes.

"My father and brother play so hopefully the weather will be okay around Christmas to maybe manage a few holes."

Thursday's win over Besiktas wasn't quite a hole-in-one, but it marked a pivotal forward step in Celtic's Europa League campaign.

Finally up and running after consecutive defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, Baur gave credit to a raucous home support.

"The fans helped a lot," he explained. "You could feel the energy. It was not just us players on the field who deserved the win – it was also everyone around the stadium and they brought the energy as well.

"It’s an unbelievable feeling as a player to have everyone pushing you and being there for you. It gives you that last percentage of energy you need at the end.

"There is always pressure to win here, to win every three days. That’s what we all want. In the last two games it wasn’t possible for us. We knew it wasn’t good enough but here we played well and deserved it."

"The win was important after some tough weeks," Baur continued. "But the belief and the way we work together as a team has always been good.

"There was never any problem with that because we always believed in ourselves. We showed how we can leave our hearts on the field and put in a shift.

"It was important to get those three points and we deserved it. Hopefully we can go forward with confidence from this game."

Despite his stellar showing on Thursday, Baur missed out on Jurgen Klopp's latest Germany squad. He made his senior international debut against Serbia last month as the former Liverpool manager had named two separate squads for four fixtures.

Klopp's group was reduced this time around, though Baur will return to the under-21s.

"I can understand," Baur said of the snub. "There are so many unbelievable players in the squad, especially in my position.

"We’re talking about guys from Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund. I just do my best and hopefully they can see I am developing and improving.

"I’m still with the under-21s for the games against Belgium and Croatia, so that will be good. European matches like Thursday can only help and I have to hope they see.

"I’m still young but I’ll keep doing my best and we’ll see what happens next time."

#2184. Sheffield Wednesday star could 'easily depart' to allow Wrexham transfer - Ipswich Town will watch

Sheffield Wednesday went through a massive overhaul of their first team squad during the summer transfer window.

The Owls completed 18 deals in the aftermath of Arise Capital finalising their takeover of the club at the beginning of May.

One of the final deals that they completed was the loan of Davis Keillor-Dunn from Wrexham, with the forward arriving until January 2027.

The 29-year-old has contributed three goals and one assist from his first nine appearances in League One.

However, if the Yorkshire outfit want to keep him on loan for the remainder of the term, then it may require some reshuffling of the squad and their other loan options due to the terms of the business plan agreed to with the EFL.

Sheffield Wednesday’s other loan options include Harry Gray, Mason Burstow, Ali Al-Hamadi, Kieran Morrison and Jaden Heskey.

When asked which loan should be terminated to make room to keep Keillor-Dunn for the second half of the season, FLW’s Sheffield Wednesday fan pundit Patrick McKenna claimed that it’s between Ali Al-Hamadi and Mason Burstow.

However, the latter has started to perform well in the last few weeks, which has put Al-Hamadi’s position at Hillsborough under significant threat, if an exit will be necessary to retain Keillor-Dunn.

“Looking at the loan players we have, I think at the minute the choice I would make would be Al-Hamadi,” McKenna told Football League World.

Sam Smith is set to miss the rest of the season, which could lead Wrexham to keep Davis Keillor-Dunn after his loan spell at Sheffield Wednesday ends

“He hasn’t had a lot of game time, he’s injured at the minute, but he hasn’t really done much this season and I think he probably would be the one you would get rid of.

“With Burstow, a few games ago I probably would’ve said I’d be happy for him to go, but in the past few games he shown what he can offer us.

“Unfortunately, for Al-Hamadi, that’s just put him ahead on the list.

#2183. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”

#2182. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.
