#2135. What Martin O'Neill told Kasper Hogh about Celtic goal drought after Besiktas

As German referee Sascha Stegemann sounded his full-time whistle, Martin O'Neill raised his right fist to the smoke-filled Glasgow sky.

Celtic's Europa League campaign was finally up and running courtesy of a frenetic 3-2 victory over Besiktas, the manager visibly relieved and triumphant in equal measure.

O'Neill usually heads straight up the tunnel after matches. Thursday evening was different. He instead made a beeline for his players before their customary walk round on the Celtic Park turf, embracing captain Callum McGregor and goalscorers Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran.

A turning point in Celtic's season? It's too early to say. But O'Neill knew for certain that failure to beat Besiktas would have rendered the remainder of Celtic's Europa League campaign meaningless. Now they have fresh hope and a platform for progress.

O'Neill insists they must build on their gutsy European victory.

"That is what we want to do, absolutely," O'Neill said. "From the European side, we have given ourselves a chance. We will have to go and win away from home and it will not be easy."

Thursday evening saw the manager make five changes to his lineup. Jordan Lotomba recorded his first start at right-back and Kasper Hogh, Sebastian Tounekti, and James Forrest made up a second string frontline.

From Forrest, O'Neill wanted experience and added defensive security. Hogh offered a focal point in attack and went off to a standing ovation in the 77th minute.

It marked his 15th Celtic appearance without a goal but the home crowd were appreciative of his work rate, as was O'Neill.

"I want centre-forwards to be able to hold it and that is what he did," O'Neill stated. "He is not Duran, he is not a dribbler. But if he can do this for us against strong opposition it will stand him in good stead.

"I think Thursday night will be good for him. I said to him that I’m not worried about whether he scores a goal.

"Of course you want centre-forwards to score and of course centre-forwards live on them. But I said to him that last night I wanted him to be strong and fight when the ball is played up to him.

"I thought in terms of holding the ball up and bringing people into the game that he did really well."

Hogh, signed from Bodo/Glimt for a club record transfer fee in excess of £11 million during the summer transfer window, had no opportunities against Besiktas.

The Dane registered just one touch in the opposition penalty area and didn't have a single shot on goal.

Hogh is being starved of the service upon which he thrived at Bodo.

To that concern, O'Neill responded: "If they are going man for man and we have gone really, really low in terms of going close to the goalkeeper then the next one in if you are dinking it in is where a centre-forward has to play.

"If it is a decent ball in then he has to hold it up because he should be first. If it is in the air and he has to fight for it then it is difficult. But if you dink it in for him then you can start from there."

"Centre-forwards need a goal," O'Neill continued. "But that performance there against European opposition will give him confidence. I don’t know what side we will play on Sunday. But this lad has scored goals in the Champions League remember.

"He will get a confidence boost from Thursday night in terms of doing that part of the game well. But it will be nice for him to score a goal."

Hogh needn't have to worry about goals if Duran maintains his apex form. The Colombian couldn't have been more influential after coming off the bench against Besiktas, netting a crucial brace to give Celtic all three points.

First, Duran latched on to Osmand's reverse pass, rounding opposition goalkeeper Alexander Nubel and slotting into an empty net. He then brilliantly controlled Kieran Tierney's wayward shot, this time beating Nubel from six yards out.

"At this minute, he is on fire," O'Neill said of Duran. "He can play wide right, he has done that. He has played wide left for his other club. But centre-forward is where he is dynamic."

When Duran plays through the middle, Hogh is often sacrificed. Conversely, Hogh starting usually sees Duran shifted to the right flank. For O'Neill, it's onerous finding the perfect balance.

"We made five changes on Thursday night because it was necessary," he explained. "The boys who came on were always going to come on after 60 minutes.

"You can’t just plan things like this. Somebody might pick up an injury. Things change during the course of the game. But the plan before it was for these lads to go on. We were always going to make the changes.

"It was necessary if we wanted a bit more gusto in the side and a bit more playing in behind. That gave the opportunity for Duran to weave a bit of magic."

Focus rightly lay on Celtic's attacking play after Thursday. Yet their defence was equally pivotal, limiting Besiktas to few opportunities of note.

Beyond a penalty and the resulting rebound, from which they scored, Vincenzo Italiano's side offered little in the way of forward penetration, struggling to break down Celtic's organised structure. It took a long-range effort from Orkun Kokcu to score their second of the evening.

"It was really pleasing and really important," O'Neill said of his team's defending. "We conceded some ground in the game which was to be expected, but I thought defensively we were really, really strong.

"When corners came in we dealt with them and we dealt with second balls as well after it was played out. The back four was terrific. Lotomba did well until he conceded the penalty."

Central defender Cameron Carter-Vickers had one of his better displays. The American made nine clearances and won all but one of his five duels. Accurate on the ball too, Carter-Vickers brought an air of stability to the backline.

He recovered ably from his performance against Falkirk last weekend, when his meek clearance led directly to Ethan Ross' opener. Carter-Vickers came off in the latter stages with a hamstring complaint, but O'Neill thinks he had a point to prove.

"It looked that way," said the Celtic boss. "I thought he was very strong. He was complaining about his hamstrings being very tight at half-time and I thought we would give him another 15 minutes.

"Of course, the game changed in that time and we were chasing the game from behind. But the lads who came on in the forward positions were always going to come on. James Forrest was never going to last the whole game.

"I thought he was outstanding, an absolute credit to the football club with what he did for us. Even defensively. Everybody worked so hard. It was really pleasing."

The key for Celtic and O'Neill is building on Thursday's thrilling victory. As the manager knows all too well, it'll count for nothing if Kilmarnock, St Mirren, and Torreense aren't beaten in the coming weeks.

#2134. Arsenal news: Arsenal vs Liverpool. Arteta targets Anfield record as Liverpool prepare for Premier League clash

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal vs Liverpool: Arsenal travel to Anfield on Sunday looking to maintain their strong start to the Premier League season and end a long wait for victory at Liverpool’s home ground.

A blistering start to the season has seen Mikel Arteta’s side win seven of their first eight league games, leaving them tied on points with Manchester City at the top of the table and six points ahead of Liverpool going into the game.

However, the Gunners have not beaten Liverpool in the Premier League at Anfield since 2012/13. Arteta will be aware that the Reds are starting to gel under Andoni Iraola.

They have won three of their last four league games after a lacklustre start and had their first league win at home this season with their 2-0 win over Brighton.

After replacing Arne Slot over the summer, Iraola brought his impressive three-year spell at Bournemouth to Anfield. However, Liverpool have struggled to adjust to the new manager, losing 3 of their first 4 league games.

But they have recently improved and are looking to play a much faster style of football. As Adrian Clarke notes, they are pressing more, not sitting back as much and wanting to attack quickly when they win the ball.

They have been the most direct attackers in the Premier League. They have pace to spare within their attack, with players like Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo providing a threat in advanced areas.

Isak comes into the game in good form after finding the back of the net six times in his first eight league games. He has scored in three successive games in the Premier League for the first time since joining the club.

Florian Wirtz will also play a key role in Liverpool’s attacking play. The German has been consistently creating chances for the team playing behind Isak in a 4-2-3-1 system. He has created nine chances against Brentford.

Arsenal will need to limit the space available to Liverpool’s forward players. Allowing Isak and Gakpo to combine freely could make an already difficult away fixture even harder.

Arsenal have had some positive news on their squad ahead of their Merseyside trip. Declan Rice and Riccardo Calafiori are both back in training.

Christos Tzolis has also trained after missing October. Noni Madueke has also not been ruled out by Arteta ahead of Sunday’s match after he missed the Fleetwood game.

They also have their own fitness issues to contend with. Iraola confirmed that Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz are both available after suffering injuries earlier in the month.

Jeramie Frimpong will be missing due to a hamstring issue but should be back after the international break. Hugo Ekitike, Geovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley are all still sidelined with longer-term injuries.

The presence of Rice will be key for Arsenal. He has been one of the best progressive midfielders in the Premier League, along with their captain, Martin Odegaard.

Despite losing just one of their last eight Premier League clashes against Liverpool, Arsenal are not as strong on the road.

The Gunners have not won any league games in their last 13 trips to Anfield. They have drawn five and lost eight. Their last win was a 2-0 victory back in the 2012/13 season.

They have also never gone 14 games unbeaten away from home in the league. That would be a great achievement.

However, there is good reason to believe they can do it. They have only conceded five clean sheets in the league this season. They have faced the least number of shots on target and the fewest expected goals.

Liverpool have also been on a strong run defensively with four clean sheets in their last six league games, so Arsenal must make their chances count.

A win would provide another key result against a direct rival, improving their position at the top of the Premier League table and finally putting an end to one of the clubs’ longest-running away day woes.

#2133. One single word which proves the Nuno era is truly dead and buried | West Ham News

Many fans feel they saw the very best, and the worst of West Ham United in the ‘game of two halves’ that unfolded before our eyes on Wednesday night.

Cardiff City’s threadbare, increasingly tiring squad no doubt helped the Hammers along the way, but the starting mindset seemed to sum up everything that was wrong with Nuno Espírito Santo’s West Ham  performances of late, and the second half recovery hopefully signposts what is to come under a less cautious Scott Parker.

One word stands out amongst all of the media interviews and comments made by the newly appointed head coach and his players after the game, which differentiates vividly the two managers’ styles. And hopefully points towards a fundamental shift now that Nuno is no longer.

High risk football: Nuno wasn’t capable of taking off the hand brake

As reported in the standard.co.uk, Scott Parker explained what he’d addressed at half time in the Cardiff dressing room.:

“Certainly out of possession, we needed to be more aggressive.“

There were tactical changes and substitutions, and we became more front-footed.

If any one word sums up the failure of the Nuno era it is that word: Risk. The cautious Portuguese manager cost the Hammers their Premier League place by trying to defend leads, throwing on defensive substitutes in frequent, vain hopes of keeping hold of a lead – and far too often set the team up to hang on rather than to score more.

And it was his insistence on doing the same this season, rather than setting out to dominate the division, that was driving home supporters to distraction and in the end cost him his job.

Whatever else, if only from from the first, brief but encouraging impressions of one half of football and from his words after, Scott Parker seems more prepared for the higher-risk football that goes with winning and dominating a campaign in this division.

His arrival was heralded by the moaners as the landing of ‘another negative coach’: Its of course early days, but that might prove to be a long way from the truth.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Parker also mentioned in his 1st interview I think, how he had often come into a club and had to work with the players who were there. Adding that you have to adapt the style of football, your approach, according to the profile of these players.

The majority of this squad in midfield and attack are skillful, quick thinking players who can play on the front foot, including Engels who showed as much for the first time.

So, I thought that was also an interesting & encouraging comment. He is obviously not going to take one beloved system and squeeze players into it, the way you desperately squeeze your last jumper into a backpack.

That is a complete change from recent past and will go down well with the whole squad.

Also in the Championship with the players we have, you must try things with the ball, otherwise you are using 60% of the ability of our WHU players, let alone all the youngsters (Austbo, Mukasa, Mayers..) who come from academies where you learn quick one-touch football, being attack minded, pressing high up, etc..

Before I was hoping Orford & Ajala might go on loan in January because whole setup in my opinion stank (sitting on benches on Saturdays, jogging around during general training – at that age?!?, absurd), but now, I hope they get to train with the 1st team, in the hope they will receive some individual attention and eventually get to play in a good footballing team.

Absolutely agree. Our focus should be attack, attack and attack fast and furious. If our Premier league holding midfielder and defense can’t stop pretty average attacking championship players then we don’t deserve promotion, we need at least a fast CF in the future so we can play down the channels and move the ball to turn the opposition defense

Ajala is quick could play off the shoulder maybe(?), but if Koppen can get an Antonio Mk II (as in slightly more skillful😊) then with this team and the assists & through balls we saw 2nd half against Cardiff, he would score a ton.

Bowen’s role under the rigid structures of the last 2 managers has been to sit out on the wing, leaving him reliant on service from others to play him in, and too easily predicted/defended. Difficult to captain a side if you’re isolated. 2nd half v Cardiff he had license to cut in and get around the pitch more. Maybe that will help the captaincy problem going forward.

Parker knows the championship he knows how to get out of this leaque it should be a lot more exciting with the way parker likes to play his record speaks volumes so.we should be firing up to top place anytime soon COYI

Parker seems to want to see us working harder to get the ball back quicker. He wants to see us to be more aggressive in all parts of the game. He wants us to attack in many different ways, crossing from the wings, passing through the opposition, playing the ball over the top, and he wants the ball moved quickly in a positive manor. Nothing negative there so get behind him and the team, lets make it work!

Much easier to take risks when you are 0-3 down. He really had no other choice at half time at Cardiff did he? I hope he continues this philosophy when it is 0-0

Nuno destroyed West Ham with his idiotic selections. It almost seemed deliberate, but I can’t fathom why. But he’s gone, move on. Come on Scotty, get us back up where we belong. COYI.

His selections was the reason why West Ham went down. He simply did not play the strongest team and keep choosing favourites.

Well said Ken West Ham fans have endured three years of pain starting with Sully war of attrition to get rid of Moyes followed by Loppy Potter and Nuno I now look forward to enjoying the new era of Scott Parker as a positive experience COYI

Parker is NOT a negative coach. By Nuno’s standards, Parker’s version of West Ham will be a breath of fresh air…..

Agressive Front-footed More direct Taking risks Energetic

All words he has used already, and we saw first hand in the 2nd half vs Cardiff.

Here’s a risk to take, take the captaincy from Bowen. Great player but not a marshall on the pitch. Since JL Bowen has been Captain and we have shown some really poor motivation on the pitch. I can imagine Parkers half time talk took him back to being a captain and injecting drive and determination in to the team. That same drive needs to be evident when he is not on the pitch, he needs to rely on a strong captain and I don’t feel that is Bowen.

4 managers now since Moyes, and no Declan or Noble, both were strong motivational Captains. It’s not all down to the manager. If Parker can look at the team and find a motivational leader, this would take pressure off Bowen. Parker should know what he is looking for

Who though, Ant, would start every game and lead by example. Only one I can see is Soucek and he doesn’t start

Maybe Parker can help Bowen understand his captains role more. Although he was never actually West Ham’s captain, that was Matthew Upson, he was captain in all but name. Certainly Bowen put in a real captains performance in that second half against Cardiff

Although my memory isn’t as good as it was, I’m sure Parker held the captaincy for a while in the team. I know he did for other clubs as I’m sure he replaces Shearer at Newcastle

I agree Martin, although Ant makes a valid point, Jared Bowen is a great player, a leader, but has not been a successful captain.

Yep granted it’s a hard choice noting who we have in the squad, another reason why we suffer due to a lack of leaders. Soucek should work if Parker wants to play him more, otherwise it will mean looking to the window for a leader on the pitch. Possibly Alvarez if he gets his chance back in the squad.

Alvarez was a shout when Rice left but it would need some diplomacy Bowen may not agree. Soucek is the obvious answer but as mentioned playing time looks to be restricted.

You don’t need to be captain to have a voice on the pitch. Bowen can continue with the official duties whilst doing what he can from the position he is in.

All of the senior figures in the side should be capable enough and encouraged to help with the leadership of our new forceful team.

The better goalkeepers also marshal the players in their box. The likes of Soucek and Alvarez successfully captain their countries and not by being the ‘best’ player but by understanding and motivating the players around them.

Yep, as I sat watching us take a lead against a woeful Derby team, my frustration grew as to why we seemed reluctant to step on their throats and finish them off. Instead we let them back in to the game due to our encouragement of ceding possession and playing the ball endlessly across the back lien and side to side in midfield. The other word that Parker used which was accurate was Passive.

yes, that word ‘passive’ really hit home for me.

#2132. Arsenal injury news: Arteta faces selection dilemma ahead of Liverpool clash

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will have a few key injury updates ahead of their clash with Liverpool on Sunday, but Mikel Arteta still has some tough choices to make in his front line.

Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori and Christos Tzolis have returned to training so there is hope they can play in the Premier League clash against Anfield.

Bukayo Saka is still out with a quad injury, but Noni Madueke looks to be fit to go into the final game. Max Dowman is also suspended after Arsenal were unable to overturn his red card suspension after the defeat to Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup.

However, Arteta has some good options to choose from. He can ill afford any more injuries in attack.

Rice’s return will be key after missing the midweek cup clash.

The midfielder was subbed in the win against Everton with a knock. His absence was a blow against Fleetwood.

He trained on Friday. As long as he does another session on Saturday, he will be available. Rice is a big boost for Arsenal in the middle of the park as they face a Liverpool side who have been in good form recently.

Calafiori is also edging closer to a return. The Italian has played in the last seven Premier League games for Arsenal but missed against Everton.

However, he was only on for a short period when he came on as a sub. But he seemed to have an issue. Arteta said that it didn’t seem like a big problem, but they’re taking some caution.

Like Rice, Calafiori trained on Friday and will be able to go to Merseyside if he finishes his session on Saturday.

Tzolis is another possible addition. The winger has missed Arsenal’s last five matches after suffering a hamstring injury while playing for Greece in October.

His latest scan showed encouraging progress, and he has now returned to training. A further successful session would put him in contention for Sunday’s match.

The main issue for Arteta will be his lack of attacking width.

Madueke did not join the squad for the trip to Fleetwood due to an ankle injury sustained in the Everton game. He did not train on Monday, but Arteta has not ruled him out of the game against Liverpool. He will have to finish his session on Saturday.

Dowman is also missing due to suspension. He was sent off in the 1-1 draw against Fleetwood after a challenge from Harrison Neal. His appeal was rejected by the FA, so he will miss the game against Liverpool.

Saka makes it even worse for the Gunners. The England international has a quad injury from the Bayern Munich game and is likely to be out for several weeks.

Arteta confirmed that he will need another scan before there is a clearer timeline for his return but is likely to be out for a long period of time.

William Saliba is still missing from the squad, having aggravated a back injury during his time playing for France at the World Cup this summer.

But the defender has returned to doing one-on-one training on the training ground.

Arsenal will perform an MRI scan to monitor his progress. Arteta has suggested there have been positive signs, and he is expected back in December.

The main talking point will be Rice, Calafiori and Tzolis returning to training ahead of Sunday.

It would give Arsenal a nice boost with all three players fit. Madueke is still a doubt and they have fewer options going forward with Saka and Dowman out.

#2131. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners target Brazilian teenager Eduardo Pape

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are increasing their interest in Cruzeiro youngster Eduardo Pape.

Despite the fact he has yet to play for the senior side in Brazil, the 17-year-old has attracted interest from a number of clubs. It is understood that Arsenal is keeping an eye on the youngster. Newcastle United and Bayern Munich are also linked with the midfielder.

The move could be a good fit with the Gunners liking to identify young talent early on. However, Pape is still very much in the early stages of his career, and any move would be seen as an investment into his future.

Arsenal are reportedly targeting Pape as a potential signing in 2027. The teenager is valued at around £33m.

Pape has already had previous experience playing for Cruzeiro’s Under-20s. He’s played 32 times and scored three goals and three assists.

He has left a successful headline in junior football as well. Pape has netted six goals in eight matches and strives for a place in the Brazilian U17 World Cup squad.

The tournament gives an opportunity to demonstrate his skills. The scouts will closely monitor the tournament, so any team interested in the player will be able to see his progress.

Of course, not just Arsenal would want to sign him. Clubs like Newcastle and Bayern Munich have already expressed interest in securing him. This is likely to cause a competitive atmosphere.

There is a concern that there hasn’t been any senior-level play from Pape. As he has never played first-team football before. It will be difficult to see how he will adapt to playing in Europe.

The contract is until December 2029, meaning Cruzeiro are in a strong position. There isn’t a huge need for the Brazilian club to rush into any decisions, meaning Pape can get some experience in a comfortable environment before moving abroad.

However, they have been very successful in the past at bringing in young Brazilian players. Gabriel Martinelli was brought in from Ituano as a teenager and has become an important first team player.

It gives us an insight into what Pape could hope to achieve.

It shows that Arsenal are looking further ahead with their recruitment. Whether they make a move for him remains to be seen. Pape will be one to keep an eye on as we approach the 2027 transfer window.

#2130. This simple fix will ‘unleash’ West Ham talent after costly Nuno cock-up | Report

West Ham United’s treatment of loanees hasn’t always been well received by their parent clubs. It’d be doubtful that Brighton would ever want to entertain sending another prospect out on loan to West Ham, after the experiences endured by Igor Julio and Evan Ferguson whose careers nosedived after they’d donned the claret and blue shirt for their photo shoots: Neither were seen again for the season.

However. this time around Manchester City must be delighted that the Irons are getting excellent value for money out of loanee Divine Mukasa, even if they weren’t utilising him to his best in Nuno’s favoured, deeper midfield role.

Manchester City fan site esteemedkompany.com, even from afar, identified that the midfielder’s deployment by Nuno as a deep lying defensive option was not playing to his strengths:

“There is an argument to be made that Nuno Espirito Santo played Mukasa out of position….

“Parker utilized Mukasa as an attacking midfielder in the match…

Mukasa scored West Ham’s first goal in a remarkable comeback

Mukasa then produced a sublime chip to beat Cardiff City keeper Yousef Salech, setting the stage for West Ham’s comeback. That goal illustrated what Mukasa can do playing in arguably his best position.….

Scott Parker may decide to unleash Mukasa as an attacking midfielder”

You’d hope that is one of the easier decisions for Scott Parker and his team to take: Mukasa already has more goals than our so-called strikers Taty and Pablo – combined. Which doesn’t say much about the other two, but surely means the young loanee’s best deployment is exactly as he finished the game against Cardiff City.

Parker has plenty of options as deeper-lying midfielders just sitting ignored by Nuno for months – blow away the cobwebs on Alvarez, Magassa (who did look rusty) or Orford and any one of the three can, with a little bit of integration, do that job and allow the hugely talented Manchester City loanee to do more of just what he’s here for.

The Mancunians didn’t watch much of the game did they? If they did they’d know who plays in goal for Cardiff…. 🧐

Good article – shame the Citeh site didn’t give our old boy Nathan Trott the credit:)

#2129. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners explore loan move for Real Madrid striker Endrick

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are keeping their options open regarding a January move for Real Madrid striker Endrick, as Mikel Arteta looks to strengthen his attacking options.

The Gunners have been in contact about a loan move for the Brazilian. There is also talk of a permanent move. However, Real Madrid are reluctant to let him leave and feel he has a big future ahead at the club.

Endrick has struggled to earn consistent game time at the Bernabeu.

While he is only 20 years old and has plenty of time left to make his mark at the top level, a new transfer away from Madrid could give him a more consistent role.

Arsenal are among the clubs keeping an eye on Endrick ahead of the January transfer window, reports TEAMtalk.

The forward was loaned to Lyon for the second half of last season to get more regular game time.

However, his representatives are said to be open to looking for another move if things do not improve in Madrid.

It seems Arsenal are interested in signing Endrick on loan with a view to making the move permanent. This will give them time to see how he settles into the Premier League.

However, Real Madrid may be in a strong position. They are still loyal to the young player and would prefer to keep him at the Spanish club.

Arsenal will rely on Madrid being more willing to let him go.

The reported interest from Arsenal comes as Arteta looks to strengthen his attacking options.

Endrick would provide variety to an attacking line-up which has been under pressure of late. His age and potential make a loan deal with an option to make the move permanent an attractive option.

There is also positivity from his previous stint with Lyon. He has already been on a loan move from Madrid and has demonstrated that he can make progress when getting regular game time.

Arsenal have previously signed young talents from Real Madrid.

Martin Odegaard came to north London as a young player after failing to make an impact in the first team at Madrid. He then became a key player for Arteta, taking on the role of captain.

Endrick will be hoping to follow a similar trajectory.

There is no suggestion that any deal is near despite Arsenal’s interest.

Endrick remains an important part of Real Madrid’s long-term plans. His representatives are thought to be looking at other options to help his career develop.

This loan deal would provide a solution for all parties. Arsenal would have another attacker to bring in, Endrick would play more regularly and Madrid would still have an interest in his future.

It will also depend on how willing the Spanish giants are to move their stance before January.

For now, Arsenal are in contact with Endrick as they consider a move. The Brazilian’s future may soon become a topic of interest ahead of the winter transfer window.

#2128. Arsenal news: Arteta’s side secure landmark victory at Anfield

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal news, Arsenal have finally found a way to win at Anfield again. Their latest victory owed as much to defensive discipline as Kai Havertz’s decisive goal.

The Gunners claimed a 1-0 Premier League victory against Liverpool, ending their 14-year wait for victory at the iconic stadium. Declan Rice set up their opener as Havertz put the visitors ahead on the 16th minute.

It was a tough afternoon for Mikel Arteta’s side as they were put under sustained pressure by their opponents. The Reds also created a number of dangerous chances throughout the match, especially in the first half.

Arsenal held their composure, and the backline was calm throughout. David Raya made the crucial interventions to keep the lead safe.

They are now three points ahead at the top of the Premier League after Manchester City lost to Brighton.

While the attack has been a key aspect of Arsenal’s title charge, they were put under pressure defensively at Anfield.

Liverpool came out aggressively after going behind. Virgil van Dijk caused problems from set pieces, and Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar from a free kick.

Raya was quick to block Van Dijk’s dangerous flick on and prevent Alexander Isak from capitalising. However, Alexis Mac Allister did head over the bar as Liverpool looked to level the game.

Arsenal were forced into another stretch as Jurrien Timber blocked well. William Saliba and Gabriel helped to limit Liverpool’s chances.

The stats tell the story of how well the visitors defended. Liverpool had 17 shots but couldn’t get one on target.

Liverpool were unable to create a shot on target for the first time in recorded history (since 2003-04) in a Premier League game at Anfield.

Meanwhile, it was the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet in the Premier League at the ground since September 2012. The result was especially important following their Carabao Cup heartbreak against Fleetwood Town earlier in the week.

Whilst they have made a great defensive stand, Arsenal’s two most influential players in the final third made the difference.

Rice won the turnover, drove down the right and played a low cross into the six-yard box. Havertz made his run to the back post and finished to give Arsenal the early lead.

The goal also takes Havertz to 46 Premier League goals, making him the most prolific German in the competition and overtaking former Manchester City midfielder Ilkay Gündogan.

Rice had a huge influence on the game. His performance in the middle of the park helped Arsenal deal with the intensity of Liverpool, and he was named man of the match.

Christos Tzolis provided an important attacking outlet. His pace created chances to ease pressure on Arsenal. He forced an incredible save from Alisson with a late first-time effort.

The win was Arsenal’s first at Anfield in any competition since September 2012 and their 300th away win in the Premier League.

Arteta’s team have had a stellar start to the season, taking 24 points from nine games. They have also proved they are capable of getting results in tough circumstances.

They will now look ahead to their Champions League game on Wednesday against Slavia Prague and then back to domestic action against Hull City.

#2127. Why One Key Name is Missing From Parker’s Back Room Team | West Ham News

All change within West Ham’s coaching set up this week.

One name that has been mentioned by supporters since Scott Parker’s arrival, yet seems missing from the Hammers new – look post Nuno back room team is Mark Robson, with questions asked as to whether he would be involved within the new coaching set up as part of Parkers’s team.

While Robson has remained part of West Ham’s coaching structure, he actually returned to his role as the Academy of Football’s Senior Professional Development Phase Coach and Under-21s Lead Coach in the summer of 2026.

Robson did work with Nuno upon the Portuguese manager’s arrival from Nottingham Forest

According to the club, this was the same position he had previously held before stepping into first-team coaching roles. His move back to the Academy coincided with changes behind the scenes following Nuno’s decision to reshape his coaching staff in the summer, including the addition of Rui Pedro Silva, who departed earlier in the week alongside Nuno and Rui Barbosa.

When Scott Parker arrived, he too preferred to work with trusted personnel, bringing long-time colleague Jonathan Hill in as Assistant Head Coach. Yet Robson’s return to the Under-21s should never be viewed as a demotion.

The Upton Park-born coach is regarded as one of the most respected development coaches in English football. After a playing career that included helping West Ham secure promotion to the Premier League in 1992/93, Robson built an impressive coaching CV across both youth and senior football.

His biography confirms that he worked with Charlton Athletic’s academy and first team, held coaching roles at Gillingham, Peterborough United and Barnet, became an FA Youth Coach Educator, and later spent several years coaching within England’s youth international set-up. He also worked at Norwich City and Aston Villa before returning to West Ham in 2021.

Perhaps most significantly, much of that career has been centred on one thing, developing young players.

West Ham’s Academy has long prided itself on producing talent capable of making the jump into the first team. In that environment, Robson’s expertise is arguably more valuable than almost any role he could occupy elsewhere within the football club.

The situation is also not entirely new. Robson similarly returned to the Under-21s in 2024 after spending the 2023/24 campaign working within the first-team coaching set-up.

West Ham have repeatedly shown a willingness to move him between senior and academy football depending on where they feel his knowledge can have the greatest impact.

With suggestions that West Ham will continue to place significant importance on producing homegrown talent, keeping one of England’s most highly regarded youth coaches with the Under-21s may be just as important as any appointment made alongside Parker in the first-team dugout.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

I was suggesting Mark Robson as an interim manager till end of season, because he obviously gets on with this players and he has them playing quick, effective football that is good to watch. The 2nd half of WHU against Cardiff with the ball moved quickly forwards with sharp passes, reminded me of the U21 style of play.

Still think there is a need to look after ex-U21s who are around the 1st team because they still need one on one coaching, to concentrate on their weaknesses. Just a few hours a week, or individual work with a 1st team player who looks after them, or an advanced academy abroad.

I look at a player such as Fearon (he is not the only one) and I think you have the type of player who with 2-3 seasons on loan and a good club (Como with Fabregas – ain’t going to happen, but..) he would come back a very accomplished and well rounded player who would be a real asset to the club. Same for all the ex-academy lads already in the squad.

Depends on manager’s approach, coaches & Koppen, plus whoever looks after loans/ongoing ex-U21 development but important phase in their development.

Not a demotion for Mark Robson, absolutely. Working with youngsters might be what he prefers as well. A lot to do, to work on and hone. also rewarding.

#2126. Arsenal injury news: Eberechi Eze concern emerges as Bukayo Saka awaits scan

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal came out on top in their match against Liverpool. Mikel Arteta admitted they have a new injury concern to deal with after Eberechi Eze was hurt. Bukayo Saka is also still out for the Gunners as they face two more games before the break.

The 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield means they are three points clear at the top of the Premier League. Arteta will need to be careful with his squad ahead of their Champions League clash against Slavia Prague on Wednesday and home game against Hull City.

Eze was a surprise omission from the starting line-up, despite featuring well in recent games.

Arteta later revealed that the England international was suffering from a problem going into the game. He also praised the club’s medical and performance team for getting him fit enough to be included in the travelling party.

There is some light at the end of the tunnel, with Eze being named on the bench. There is uncertainty over whether he will be available for the trip to Prague.

Arsenal will look to train him to see if he can play against Slavia. However, Arteta’s comments suggest that the issue is significant enough that he couldn’t start against Anfield despite his recent form.

There is positive news on Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori. All three were able to overcome their fitness concerns to start the game against Liverpool and play the full 90 minutes.

The availability of these players provides Arteta with more options as he heads into a busy week. However, he will be keen to avoid any unnecessary risk to those that have only just returned to full fitness.

Saka is still the biggest injury concern for Arsenal as he has failed to play for the last three games after suffering a quad injury in the clash against Bayern Munich.

He was forced off after just 10 minutes of the Champions League draw. He will not be available for the fixtures against Slavia Prague and Hull.

There were concerns that Saka may miss up to eight weeks of action. Arteta hasn’t confirmed when he will be back on the pitch.

The Arsenal manager explained earlier that there was a need to scan Saka again to see how the fluid around the injury was behaving. The medical staff will also want to know if there has been any damage to the tendon.

This will give clearer information on when he will be able to return to play. Until then Arsenal will have to plan without one of their most important attacking players.

Another player looking to make his way back to fitness is William Saliba. The defender has not played this season after aggravating a back issue during his time playing for France at the World Cup.

However, he has avoided surgery and has been back in individual outdoor training at the club’s training ground recently. Arteta says there are positive signs that his recovery is going well.

The club plan for an MRI scan to see how he is recovering. They are hoping to get him back in December, but it has not been confirmed by Arsenal.

It would give Arteta a huge boost to his defensive options. For now he will have to keep monitoring his recovery.

They play Slavia Prague on Wednesday and then play Hull at home on Saturday. This gives them two more chances to build up their position ahead of the international break; however, Arteta will have to consider the latest medical reports.

Claret & Hugh has received fresh information from a West Ham United club insider clarifying how Scott Parker was selected as the Hammers’ new head coach, including a categorical denial that former assistant coach Johnny Heitinga was ever in contention for the job.

A number of names were considered following the decision to dismiss Nuno Espírito Santo, but we understand that Parker was the only candidate put forward by chief executive Karim Virani. His record of winning promotion from the Championship, combined with his knowledge of West Ham and its culture, made him the clear frontrunner from the outset.

Crucially, our source has confirmed that Parker was the unanimous first choice of the entire West Ham board, rather than a compromise appointment reached after disagreements over alternative candidates.

John Heitinga was not interviewed for the Hammers job

However, a club insider has told Claret & Hugh:

“There were no talks with Jonny Heitinga and he was not under consideration.”

The clarification is significant because it rules out Heitinga as a candidate, rather than simply suggesting that West Ham preferred Parker.

It also provides further detail about the appointment process. As Claret & Hugh revealed on Monday, Parker had emerged as the leading contender shortly after Nuno’s dismissal, although his appointment had not yet been finalised.

We subsequently reported details of Parker’s promotion-linked contract arrangements, reflecting the board’s determination to secure an immediate return to the Premier League.

The latest information makes clear that, while other names were considered during the process, Parker was the candidate backed by Virani and unanimously supported by West Ham’s directors.

#2123. Arsenal transfer news: Arteta considers January moves for two highly rated attackers

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could have two ambitious attacking signings in mind for January. Eli Junior Kroupi and Kenan Yildiz are reportedly attracting Mikel Arteta’s attention.

Both players have emerged as potential targets as the Gunners consider further changes to their forward line. However, Arsenal may face a battle to prise either youngster away from their current club.

Kroupi is already familiar with the Premier League after making an impressive start to life at Bournemouth. The forward arrived from Lorient and scored 13 goals in 35 appearances across all competitions during his first season in England.

His development was halted by a broken foot in pre-season which required an operation to fix and kept him out of action for around three months.

The 20-year-old has now returned to the Bournemouth squad and has played as a substitute in their last three games. He will be hoping to get more game time as he gets back into full fitness.

Arsenal were linked with a move for Kroupi in the summer. His return to action has reignited interest in the player. A number of other European clubs also understood to be watching his situation.

Kroupi has attracted interest from a variety of top clubs including Manchester United, Tottenham, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

The French Under-21 international has impressed with his goal scoring in his first campaign in England. At only 20 years old, he has plenty of development to do under an experienced manager like Arteta.

However, Bournemouth are said to be reluctant to let Kroupi leave in January. Selling a bright young forward would leave Marco Rose with a tough decision to make.

It could get even more complicated if Alex Scott is also being seriously pursued. Chelsea and Liverpool are both linked with the midfielder.

Arsenal may therefore struggle to convince the Cherries to part with Kroupi during the winter window.

Another exciting option for Arsenal comes in the form of Juventus winger Yildiz. The winger has been linked with a move to North London for a number of transfer windows. He has once again been in the news recently at the end of the summer.

However, the Turkish international has struggled to get going on this campaign. He has only featured once in Serie A and has failed to feature since he suffered an injury.

Juventus have previously shown little interest in letting him leave. Head coach Luciano Spalletti firmly dismissed the prospect during the summer. Indicating that even an offer worth €100 million would not change the club’s position.

However, things could change next season. There are reports from Italy that Juventus may have to sell their star player if they fail to make the Champions League.

The Turin-based outfit are currently sitting in seventh spot in Serie A after just 10 games and are six points away from the qualifying spots.

This means that if they don’t make it into Europe, then it could put more pressure on Arsenal’s pursuit of Yildiz. It could create more pressure on them to raise funds.

Arsenal had a very busy summer with the addition of Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa, Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier.

But they also missed out on a few big names, such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez.

Despite this, there is still interest in Kroupi and Yildiz, suggesting that Arteta is still looking to strengthen his attacking options. Both players would bring quality and potential to the squad; however, there are some issues with both.

There are many unknowns surrounding this situation. Bournemouth aren’t keen to sell Kroupi and Juventus aren’t in a great financial position.

This doesn’t mean that either player will definitely be moving to the Emirates but much will depend on what happens at their clubs in the coming months.

#2122. Arsenal U19s face tough Slavia Prague test in UEFA Youth League

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal’s under-19s face a significant challenge when they travel to Czechia to take on Slavia Prague in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday.

The young Gunners have picked up four points from their first three games and will be hoping to build on that in the league phase. Two wins would definitely help their chances of getting into the knockout stages.

They kicked off their campaign with a win against Napoli and put on a great show in a 3-3 draw against Bayern Munich last month.

Those results have left them 18th in the standings, 16 places below their next opponents. With the top 22 teams progressing to the knockout stages, another positive result could prove important for their qualification hopes.

However, Slavia Prague has made a much stronger start and will provide a difficult examination for David Horseman’s side.

Slavia have won all three of their first games in the UEFA Youth League and are sitting in second place. Just behind Real Madrid on goal difference.

They began well with a 2-1 win against French side Lens. They then went on to beat Sabah 3-0 and then put in another strong display against Fenerbahce.

Despite falling behind in Prague, the players fought back to win the game 3-1. The three wins means Slavia are already past the number of points they scored last season in the league stage.

They also advanced to the knockout stages last time, finishing 20th before they faced Benfica.

Mubarak Suleiman put the team ahead twice, but they were pegged back by two goals in the last 30 minutes as their European run came to an end.

This season they have looked like a much stronger team. With a perfect record, they will be one of the hardest teams that Arsenal will face.

The meeting on Wednesday provides an opportunity for Arsenal to get revenge for their heavy defeat in Prague last season.

The two sides met during the 2025/26 league campaign, with Slavia winning 5-1 at home.

Arsenal were three goals down at the break after an own goal plus goals from Bartosz Szywala and Jakub Kolisek.

O’Neill pulled one back after the break, but the home side had the final word as Suleiman and Matej Kotrba scored in stoppage time.

This loss shows how tough it will be for Horseman’s side. Slavia have already proven their attacking prowess against Arsenal and are playing even better in this campaign.

The young Gunners will have to play much more disciplined if they are to leave Prague with three points.

Arsenal fans can watch the UEFA Youth League clash on Wednesday.

It will be streamed via the Arsenal app and Arsenal.com, with the match taking place at the Sports Centre Radotin.

Updates will also be posted here and on the club’s Academy X page.

A full match report, highlights and post-match interviews with Horseman and one of the young players will be published on Arsenal’s official channels.

With them still in contention to qualify for the knockout stages, Arsenal will be looking to get off to a good start. Slavia’s great early start means they will have to play some of their best football of the tournament.

#2120. Fulham v Newcastle United preview ahead of Premier League clash

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Welcome to the Fulham v Newcastle United preview.

Saturday 7th November and a 3pm kick-off.

Newcastle United travel to London this weekend looking to draw a line under a disastrous double defeat in League and Cup to Everton, that has the potential to derail our season before it’s really got started.

The Toon will be hoping to get their season back on track before a tedious international break is followed by a make or break run of fixtures that may very well define the campaign.

Despite this being our thirteenth match of 2026-27, this will be only our second game of the season not selected for live TV. Meaning we can enjoy the comparative luxury of a Saturday 3pm kick-off and travelling Toon fans should have plenty of time to enjoy before and after the match…fingers crossed they’ll enjoy the actual match itself as well!

Newcastle have won two and lost four of their past six league matches as a decent start to the season has disintegrated to an alarming degree. Wins have come against Hull City and Crystal Palace but terrible defeats against four ordinary teams in the shape of Leeds, Coventry, Villa and Everton have seen the Toon drop a very achievable twelve points. We’ve scored six goals in these six matches but conceded a whopping eleven and only kept one clean sheet. The six points gained has us languishing in thirteenth position but a reflection of a bang average league means we could squeeze into the top seven this weekend should all results go our way.

Fulham have won two, drawn three and lost one of their past six league games. Victories have come against Coventry and Hull whilst they’ve drawn with Liverpool, Man United and Aston Villa. Their loss came away at Ipswich. They’ve scored five goals in these games and conceded four. They currently sit fifteenth in the league despite a dreadful start to the season that saw them take just two points from their first six matches. A win at the weekend would see them leapfrog the Toon and could see them as high as eighth depending on results elsewhere.

Newcastle hosted Everton on Monday night and were left deeply disappointed by a second defeat to the Toffees in just five days. The first half was a complete non-event with United looking and playing like an away team, barely getting out of their own half let alone troubling old nemesis Jordan Pickford. We were lucky to go into the half-time break goalless but the Blues broke the deadlock early on in the second period to leave the Toon desperate for a goal. As the Black and Whites finally woke up, it looked like an equaliser was secured when Elanga prodded the ball past Pickford at the back post. Unfortunately it rebounded off the upright, spun on the line and was hacked away to safety. Newcastle continued to push for a leveller but only really created a couple of decent chances, Wissa having a shot saved and Ramsey smashing an effort just wide. Unfortunately Ramsey also found the time to pick up two equally ludicrous yellow cards late on to ensure he received a red card and now has to serve a suspension to cap what was a miserable night for NUFC.

Fulham travelled to Aston Villa last weekend and were grateful for an absolute goalkeeping howler as they achieved a 1-1 draw. Behind at the break, Fulham were gifted an equaliser in the second half when the Villa ‘keeper dropped the ball over the line to ensure both sides would be able to enjoy a share of the points.

Newcastle have played three matches in London this season and won all of them without conceding a goal.

The Toon have lost their last two visits to Fulham.

NUFC have scored fourteen goals in their last seven games at Craven Cottage.

In 2003-04 Sir Bobby Robson was once again attempting to mastermind a return to the Champions League for his United side that had endured a difficult start to the season. An October trip to Fulham gave the Toon the opportunity to win their third match in a row but things got off to a disastrous opening when old boys Lee Clark and Louis Saha both found the net early on to give Fulham a two goal lead after just eight minutes. Thankfully this double setback spurred United into life and they gained a toe-hold in the match when Laurent Robert scored soon after with a half-volley. NUFC saved the real drama and excitement for the start of the second half when Alan Shearer twice found the net in front of incredulous away supporters. Our number nine kept his nerve to bury a spot-kick that brought the scores level after Ameobi was fouled in the area but even better to come. A few minutes after the equaliser, great link-up play with Jermain Jenas allowed Shearer the chance to put the Toon ahead and he made no mistake, rifling the ball into the roof of the net to send the travelling Toon Army delirious. Whilst this was undoubtedly one of the highlights of the season, it was also our last league victory away from home that campaign. Just two wins on our travels throughout the whole campaign meant that United would just miss out on a place in the Champions League. Fulham 2-3 Newcastle.

Philippe Albert is an absolute legend for those of us lucky enough to grow up in the mid-nineties. Signed by Kevin Keegan after a number of impressive performances at the 1994 World Cup, Albert soon proved that there was so much more than just defending to his game. Never afraid to bomb forward, he was often found at the other end of the pitch to good effect scoring a number of important goals. Although he’s best remembered for his sublime chip to end the scoring in a famous 5-0 victory over Man United, a personal favourite memory of mine is when he galloped forward to volley home an equally special effort in a 3-3 draw against Man City the previous season. Keegan was so impressed by Albert at Newcastle that he signed him again for Fulham in 1998 and was rewarded with two goals as the cottagers gained promotion from the second tier.

Louis Saha played on loan at Newcastle under Ruud Gullit in 1999 but managed only a handful of games. His only league strike came in a 4-1 home win against Coventry. He also netted a cracker away at Blackburn in the fifth round of the FA Cup. His winning goal set up a quarter-final tie with Everton as the Toon marched on to the Wembley final. He signed for Fulham in 2000 and scored over fifty league goals for the club, he was top scorer in the promotion campaign of 00/01 and was named in the PFA team of the year. He spent four years at Craven Cottage before moving on to Man United.

Danny Guthrie signed for the Toon in 2008 and spent four years on Tyneside, enduring the low of relegation in 2009 to the high of a top five Premier League finish in 2012. He was an integral part of our promotion in 2009-10, netting five goals and providing thirteen assists as we won the Championship. He played for Fulham on loan in 2015 but failed to find the net in six league appearances.

Matthias Jaissle after a 1-0 defeat at home to Everton: “They trained at a high level in the build-up, but when the ref started the game you couldn’t see that. It wasn’t the plan to shoot the long balls, it’s important to say that. It was not good enough and it was not brave enough to penetrate the last line. The goal came from an unforced error that led to a free-kick, but to be honest we were just sleeping. It’s so easy for them to take the quick free-kick and we were surprised. On a good day of course, Hornicek saves it. We have to stick together now, we have to show unity. It’s the only way. When the goals aren’t coming easily you lack confidence, it’s normal as a human being. We saw during the week that the quality is there but we need to take it to the pitch. It’s clear I have the responsibility to make it work as the manager of this club.”

Alvaro Arbeloa after a 1-1 draw away to Aston Villa: “I’m pleased with the team’s performance, especially in the second half. We were more aggressive, we controlled the tempo of the game, we had so many chances to score some goals, but in the end we couldn’t take the chances. I am happy because we knew before the match how difficult it would be to win here. Man City lost here one week ago and they are a Champions League team with a fantastic coach so, for me I’m really proud of my players because they showed ambition and character, and we played our way, which is the most important thing.”

As it is an away match, Newcastle United fans will not be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end, for the food bank. However, you can still help out and all online cash donations are very much appreciated. For further info and/or to donate to the food bank online.

This is a tough one to call. Newcastle have been desperately poor recently whilst Fulham have achieved some decent results after a poor start to their season. I’m old enough to remember the days when we couldn’t buy a win in London until a glorious night at Highbury in 2001 so have been delighted to see us achieve three wins in the capital already this season. Unfortunately, I don’t think this weekend will see a fourth. A poor game will see both teams having to be content with a point apiece. Fulham 0-0 Newcastle.

#2118. Arsenal handed major William Saliba injury boost ahead of Manchester City showdown

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have received a significant boost with William Saliba returning to first-team training. He’s spent almost four months out with a back injury.

The French international was seen returning to training on the pitch. Sparking hope that he could be back in action soon for Mikel Arteta.

Saliba has been sidelined since he suffered the injury in France’s 2-0 semi-final defeat to Spain. The defender was forced off after only 30 minutes after playing the full 90 in his previous five starts at the tournament.

The player was confirmed by Arsenal to be sidelined for a lengthy period of time in July. He did not require surgery, meaning he can begin working back into action.

His latest progress comes at an important point in Arsenal’s season, with several major fixtures approaching.

The 25-year-old has travelled to the Czech Republic with Arsenal’s squad to face Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba had played for 45 minutes in a behind-closed-moors game last week as part of his rehab.

He then returned to full first team training on Tuesday, providing another defensive option for the club.

Arteta spoke ahead of the game against Slavia Prague. He said that Saliba is happy with his recovery and is at a point where he will be used if needed.

The Arsenal manager has not confirmed if the Frenchman will be involved tonight.

Saliba has not played in a competitive game since losing to Spain in the World Cup semi-final for France. So it will be his first involvement in a competitive game since the summer.

Arsenal have coped well with Saliba’s absence.

Gabriel initially partnered Cristhian Mosquera at centre-back before the Spaniard suffered an ankle injury. This allowed Ezri Konsa to come into the starting line-up.

Ezri Konsa settled into a partnership with the Brazilian. He joined from Aston Villa for £51 million in the summer.

The partnership has helped the Gunners to have the best defensive record in the Premier League. Having only conceded 5 goals in their first 9 games.

Now that Saliba is available, Arteta has more options and flexibility with his defenders.

The manager has had past success with Saliba and Gabriel as his first-choice central defensive pairing. Their understanding has played a big part in Arsenal’s defensive displays.

However, Konsa has provided Arteta with another selection dilemma to consider when Saliba is back to full fitness.

Arsenal have a busy schedule ahead after today’s Champions League game at Slavia Prague.

On Saturday they play Hull City, followed by games against Manchester City, Real Madrid and Tottenham after the international break in November.

If Saliba can come back in, it will give Arteta more defensive options to play with, but they won’t want to rush him back.

The defender played 50 times last season, helping Arsenal win the Premier League and reach the Champions League final. He also ranked 29th in the men’s Ballon d’Or in October.

His return to training is a major step in his road to full fitness, but it remains to be seen if he will play against Slavia Prague tonight.

#2117. Sullivan Sidelined As West Ham’s Parker Decision Revealed

Claret & Hugh can reveal today that, despite reports to the contrary, David Sullivan had no input into the decision to appoint Scott Parker as West Ham United’s new manager.

Some reports in the national media have suggested that Sullivan reacted to the Hammers’ back-to-back defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion by convincing the board to sack Nuno Espírito Santo and appoint Parker. However, information received by C&H indicates that this was not the case.

Instead, we understand that the decision was driven by West Ham chief executive Karim Virani, who, following meetings on Monday, approached the board for permission to dismiss Nuno and appoint Parker. The former Hammers midfielder was already the preferred candidate, with one club insider describing him to us today as “the perfect fit”.

And it has very much been Virani liaising with Daniel Kretinsky which has prompted the club to change direction so quickly.

Karim Virani was the driving force behind the appointment of Scott Parker

The concern surrounding Nuno’s position had been building for some time and was not simply a reaction to two disappointing results. There was growing dissatisfaction within the club over performances across a number of matches, with the defeat to West Bromwich Albion effectively proving to be the last straw.

Virani subsequently decided to act more quickly than originally anticipated, with performances showing no sign of improvement. As Claret & Hugh revealed earlier this week, Monday’s meeting brought forward a dismissal which had initially been expected to come after further consideration.

Parker was very much at the top of the list, and Virani sought the board’s approval to proceed with the change. Our latest information makes an important distinction between the board approving the appointment and Sullivan personally driving the decision.

Far from being a Sullivan-led intervention following the Southampton and West Brom defeats, C&H understands that it was Virani who took the initiative to end Nuno’s tenure and bring Parker back to West Ham.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Of course Sullivan would like people to think he’s not involved and not making the decisions. Then he gets off Scot free doesn’t he.

Can’t believe that a chief executive Virani is now the man making the decisions about sacking a manager. How have we got into a position where we have owners that are not personally driving what happens in their own club. Soon as Sullivan and Kretinsky get out of our club the better.

I heard that David Sullivan had advised Karim to make this change now.

We have already read all about how Sullivan resigned from the board of West Ham the football club, he doesn’t have any operational say!

He is only a board member of holding company, and can override special resolutions.

A majority shareholder has no say in who manages his club/investment whatever your views about Sullivan this is one very bizzare story….

Good. Sideline Sullivan and you’re in with some chance of a sensible and timely decision. The number one aim is to get back to the premier league for financial reasons and Parker has to be your number one choice for attaining that aim. Correct decision at the correct moment, nothing at all like Sullivan. What happens in the premier league is only an issue if you actually get there.

#2116. Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal: Madueke and Gyokeres fire Gunners to Champions League victory

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal moved up to third in the Champions League table after beating Slavia Prague 2-1 at the Fortuna Arena.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after nine minutes, finishing calmly after Viktor Gyokeres sent him through on goal.

The Swedish striker then doubled Arsenal’s advantage with an excellent finish in the 38th minute. However, a much stronger second-half performance from Slavia made for an uncomfortable finish.

Wiktor Nowak scored a late goal to put pressure on the Gunners. They held on to take all three points.

Mikel Arteta made six changes from the Liverpool win on Sunday. William Saliba returns to the squad after his back injury.

The defender was left on the bench, with Ezri Konsa playing alongside Gabriel Magalhães in central defence.

Arsenal started brightly and took control of the game when they won the long ball forward. Gyokeres beat his man and found Madueke with a clever through ball.

The winger used his pace to get into the penalty area before sliding his finish through goalkeeper Nazar Domchak’s legs.

Arsenal continued to create chances, with Mikel Merino going close on several occasions. Domchak also produced an important save to deny the midfielder from close range.

Merino eventually helped Arsenal extend their lead. After winning possession in the Slavia half, Declan Rice found Gyokeres, who exchanged passes with the Spaniard before curling a superb finish into the far corner.

The visitors could have added a third before the break. Gabriel’s header from a corner was cleared off the line.

Arsenal appeared to be in control at half-time.

But Slavia upped the tempo and started to create more space, forcing Arsenal into a defensive stance. Early on, Oskar Kubiak fired a long-range shot, forcing David Raya to push it away.

Arteta got increasingly frustrated as Arsenal struggled to hold on to the ball and dominate the midfield.

They tried to keep pressing, but Arsenal struggled to create much at the other end. Madueke did get into a good position to shoot from an angle but didn’t have enough power to cause any problems for Domchak.

Slavia were denied a goal when Gabriel headed the ball away from the goal line. Raya made a brilliant stop to keep the shot out while the penalty area was crowded.

The Arsenal keeper made another stunning save as Kubiak powered a header from a cross. Raya deflected the ball onto the post to keep his team ahead by two goals.

Slavia scored their breakthrough goal in the 90th minute after David Jurasek played a low cross from the left. Nowak was able to run into the box to score past Raya.

It created a nervy few minutes of added time as Arsenal had to defend their lead.

Slavia could find no way back into the game as Stepan Chaloupek headed wide and Mikulas Konecny threatened in the dying moments, but his effort lacked confidence as Raya made light work of saving.

Arsenal secured their third win in their last four Champions League games to move to 10 points and into third place in the group stage.

The Gunners have now gone unbeaten in their last ten Champions League away games to set a new club record.

However, Arteta will be looking for a much better display from his side when they resume action in the Premier League against Hull City on Saturday.

#2115. Hammers outcasts no longer | Training hint suggests a new direction for Scott Parker’s West Ham

Blackburn Rovers await West Ham United tomorrow, with a second long trip within three days. According to local news outlets, the Irons squad is flying to Blackpool Airport this afternoon rather than endure another gruelling coach journey.

After the 450 mile midweek journey to Cardiff, going by road would have meant the West Ham teams’ tired bodies would have faced the even longer 490 mile round trip to Ewood Park – probably five hours each way – hardly the best preparation after minimal recovery.

However, a two week international break beckons during which time Scott Parker can really start to work on his tactics without the irritations of a game to interrupt his progress.

From the Hammers’ PR images released ahead of the Blackburn game, it is clear that this new broom has swept very clean in all corners of the training ground: Several players banished by Nuno are evidently now off the naughty step and, if appearances are anything to go by, are loving life under their new boss.

Maxwel Cornet, the forgotten man under successive managers, evidently got some 1:1 time with his new coach:

Presumably new West Ham manager Scott Parker is pointing out directions to the medical centre

Edson Alvarez, similarly, looks energised and content with his lot which suggests he’s in a better place now that his nemesis Nuno Espírito Santo has departed the training centre.

And one look at Alphonse Areola’s expression says it all. Training has just taken on a new dimension for the French former number three who hasn’t featured in a West Ham side since well before relegation: Parker’s chosen shot stopper at Fulham, remember.

Areola – does that smile reveal that he knows something we don’t for the starting XI tomorrow? We can but hope: I’ll wager that’s a “yes”

After Scott Parkers’ selection of a rusty Soungutou Magassa as a defensive midfielder on Wednesday, the smart money might be on another similar selection involving Magassa or Alvarez tomorrow: That would certainly account for the Mexican’s more upbeat demeanour during the training session and might even please a certain vocal selection of the fan base who have been long advancing the Mexican as the solution to the Hammers’ midfield problems.

Cannot wait for the team sheet to be honest, as the Parker revolution gets into full swing. Team news here at 13.45 tomorrow.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

One of the things about NES is his behaviour was detrimental to the club and very harmful to all the (younger) players – both facts made me come to despise the man, apart from the fact did not trust him either: re. academy which he said to encourage to appease fans, while they never played except Orford 20 minutes out of position.

How do you make it get a 450 mile round trip to Cardiff?

“How do you make it get a 450 mile round trip to Cardiff?”

Start the trip 225 miles from Cardiff and then return to the starting point…. 😄

This is going to be a conondrum for Parker. Alvarez, Magassa, Cornet, Ajala, Soucek, Bioro, Aerolo, Orford this truly gives Parker a full squad. Left back options Scarles, Boiro, Mayers, Cornet. Great problem to have.

Mayers looked good… Austbo on the left. Bowen as a 10, and play Pablo as a 9 to continually press and pay Solomon on the right. Then switch Pablo at some point if he runs out of energy. Don’t we have any academy forwards? Kante making runs into the box from midfield
